book_viii.label: BOOK VIII
book_viii.title: The furnace beneath the ash bridge

yue_mother.name: Lin Yue's Mother
yue_mother.title: Worker of the west village kiln

foundry_arrival_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_001.text: Three days beyond the crossing, Lin Yue found the ash bridge by its sound. Water struck the settling shelves below; above, ceramic chimneys clicked as their cooling skins contracted. She had expected a mountain gate. The cultivation workshop began with a woman sweeping spilled charcoal from a road. Yue set down her pack and helped before asking whether the northern commission still offered paid places. Her first arm pair stayed quiet beneath her sleeve. She had carried it through the hills without asking it to carry her.

foundry_arrival_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_002.text: The sweeper pointed to a notice fixed beneath a roof tile. Rain had blurred the promised training hours, but the meals and ordinary wages remained legible. Yue read the whole sheet twice. Applicants supplied their last examination record, disclosed any route injury and worked a trial shift before joining a practice bench. Nobody promised a breakthrough. She liked that less than she liked the words about rice. Wanting the fourth stage had already begun making ordinary terms look like a delay.

foundry_arrival_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_003.text: Inside the first bay, an annealing cup stood cracked from mouth to foot. Its fracture was thin as a hair until the examiner turned it against the window. 'An excellent vessel,' the examiner said, 'until someone preferred the flattering view.' She introduced herself as Su Yan, a ninth-stage practitioner employed to inspect small furnaces and apprentice routes. Her work apron was grey with old ash. She wore no crown of flame, and the chamber behind her was cooling with its shutters closed.

foundry_arrival_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_004.text: Su Yan asked for the sluice record before asking about the river. Yue laid out the pages Duan Zhi had signed: reserve tests, compatible fractions, interruption limits and the instrument fault that had cost eleven days of rest. The examiner lingered over the fault. 'Who measured your hands afterward?' Yue named the independent healer. 'Good. A story about perseverance cannot tell me whether those two fingers recovered.' Su Yan set the river letters aside. Useful work elsewhere did not replace an anatomical examination.

foundry_arrival_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_005.text: Yue opened her lower field only for a small resting comparison. The familiar inward warmth followed its quiet route; the return met it at the hand without a rush. Su Yan watched an unpowered thread laid alongside the cuff. Then she removed it, waited, and asked Yue to repeat the observation without the comforting instrument. The second result felt weaker. Yue admitted that before the examiner uncovered the reference stone. Both observations were ordinary for the room's changing morning temperature.

foundry_arrival_006.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_006.text: On the slate, Su Yan drew two circles of equal diameter. She shaded only a narrow segment of the first. 'This is the quantity you retained. This is the fraction that your route can use without grit. The outline is not a claim that every part inside it belongs in your body.' Yue recognized the distinction. At the sluice she had learned its numbers. The foundry would ask whether she remembered it while looking at beautiful materials that promised more than copper.

foundry_arrival_007.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_007.text: A copper strip lay beside a violet glass wafer. Su Yan let Yue compare their surfaces with ordinary fingertips before either received a trace. The wafer seemed finer, colder and more deserving of a serious cultivator. 'Which will you buy?' 'I do not know its compatibility,' Yue answered. Su Yan smiled only after the answer. The strip was rated for Yue's current practice; the violet glass came from an unreconciled batch. Price and beauty had given it no permission to touch her route.

foundry_arrival_008.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_008.text: The trial shift began at the ash channel. Yue carried baskets of spent ceramic shells while two workers scraped their clean edges for reuse. She was forbidden to reinforce the carry. The path crossed a wet turn, and the ordinary load was already close to her wrist's safe working weight. She divided it into smaller trips. By noon, another applicant had passed her twice with a higher stack. Yue kept counting the baskets she could set down without shaking.

foundry_arrival_009.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_009.text: At lunch the quicker applicant laughed at his own blister. He had wanted the foreman to notice him and now could not close his hand around a spoon. Yue shared the handle of a clean cloth rather than offering qi. The foreman sent him to the wash station and paid the work he had completed. She did not call the injury a lesson earned through courage. Yue found that more unsettling than a reprimand. A place could notice effort without rewarding its most damaging form.

foundry_arrival_010.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_010.text: The ordinary meal contained barley, greens and a piece of bean curd browned against the oven wall. No pill lifted Yue's hunger away. She ate slowly, then copied her morning load into the examination book. Her hand remained normal; her shoulder was tired. Those facts occupied different columns. Beyond the table, several senior students discussed Foundation compression. Their words rose over her bowl like distant bridges. She wanted to join that conversation so fiercely that she nearly forgot to finish eating.

foundry_arrival_011.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_011.text: Su Yan returned after the furnaces' noon shutters closed. 'What did the trial shift teach you about your reserve?' Yue began with the number she expected to retain that evening. The examiner shook her head. 'We have not measured that yet. What did it teach you now?' Yue looked at her ordinary fatigue column. 'That wishing for a higher stage changes what I am tempted to omit.' The answer won no mark. It did make the next measurement less likely to inherit a lie.

foundry_arrival_012.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_012.text: The foundry admitted her to a paid bench place for six weeks, with extensions discussed before the term ended. Food, a dry bed and ordinary shifts came from the workshop account. Training fuel had a separate weekly allowance. An apprentice could spend that allowance quickly and learn nothing; she could not turn an empty socket into a debt against next month's meals. Yue pressed her thumb beside the terms and received a key with a chipped wooden tag. The key opened a drawer, not a secret realm.

foundry_arrival_013.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_013.text: Her bed stood in a room above the cooling trough. When a chimney contracted, a soft knock traveled through the floorboards. Yue unpacked her bowls, examination cord and repaired work tablet. She kept the pendant wrapped. No crisis required its offered memory, and nobody at the foundry had asked to hear it. Before sleep, she counted the copper she could spare for a return journey. Cultivation had become possible partly because she no longer confused staying with being unable to leave.

foundry_arrival_014.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_014.text: At dawn she woke before the bell and found another apprentice already boiling water. The young man's fingers were blue with ordinary pigment from marking ceramic seams. He asked what stage she held; she answered three. He answered two, then waited for the disappointment that did not come. His name was Zhen, a temporary worker studying after his shifts. Yue remembered the years in which any measured trace would have seemed impossible. She passed him the kettle and asked which cup leaked.

foundry_arrival_015.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_015.text: The leaking cup belonged to nobody's practice circuit. Its foot had warped in a shelf too close to the furnace mouth. Zhen knew where the fault lay because he had spent three days sorting failures. Yue examined it and could not make the same judgment until he showed her the uneven contact. He had a lower realm and a skill she lacked. The realization relieved her, then stung. She had begun treating progress as a ladder on which every higher foot must stand above every lower hand.

foundry_arrival_016.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_016.text: The first teaching bell gathered eight apprentices around a cold kiln. Su Yan placed the firing schedule on its lid, then folded it away. 'Name the source of its heat.' Charcoal, one student answered. Stored stones, said another. 'For this kiln, charcoal. For the adjoining chamber, a measured stone charge. For neither, my willingness to stand nearby.' They inspected the fuel bins and sockets separately. A cultivator could adjust an allowed command without pretending her body was the energy source of an entire building.

foundry_arrival_017.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_017.text: Yue's bench had a physical discharge strip beside its practice tile. She traced the escape route with an unpowered stylus before setting down her cuff. The strip met a sand pot grounded through copper mesh, well away from the annealing cups. Su Yan showed how to inspect its underside for ash paste. Water and fine ash could make a bridge that the clean top concealed. Yue remembered the salt fault at the sluice. A remembered failure gave her a question, not immunity from its cousin.

foundry_arrival_018.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_018.text: The examiner assigned no second-pair work that morning. Yue would first repeat her existing route under the foundry's conditions: dry heat, powdered mineral dust and the ordinary strain of paid handling. The prescription felt like going backward. Su Yan asked her to name the last tested environment. Yue named the damp sluice and sheltered river work. 'Your body traveled. Your examination did not automatically travel with it.' The first week would establish what she could still do here before asking what else she might learn.

foundry_arrival_019.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_019.text: At the window, an advanced student drew a bright line through a sealed glass tube. The line divided without breaking, feeding two tiny test lamps. Yue looked long enough to miss her own blank. Su Yan covered the neighboring tube with a cloth. 'That circuit belongs to its operator's assessment. You have a blank to observe.' Yue started again, cheeks hot. Her first mistake at the foundry was not an ambitious pulse. It was letting someone else's impressive work occupy the attention needed for her small task.

foundry_arrival_020.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_020.text: The covered reference gave her a usable result after the distraction passed. Yue wrote the missed first reading rather than replacing it with the second. Beside it she marked the cause she actually knew: attention left the bench. She could not claim that the neighboring lamp had interfered with her route merely because both events happened together. Su Yan read the note and placed a fresh blank beside it. The record was good enough to support another attempt precisely because it preserved a failure.

foundry_arrival_021.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_021.text: An afternoon wind carried dust through the shutters. Su Yan ended the route session and sent the students to ordinary inspection tables. Several protested that their reserves were still ample. The examiner held a clean cloth against the window; violet grit accumulated along its fibers. Quantity in a lower field did not determine the compatibility of everything entering it. Yue watched the dust without imagining that closing the shutters alone would settle the source. The kiln yard contained materials she had not yet learned to distinguish.

foundry_arrival_022.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_022.text: Zhen sorted the windborne powder with a wet brush and three ceramic wells. Ordinary black ash settled first. A violet fraction clung to the glaze; a pale mineral fraction dissolved. He had learned that separation while making furnace marks. Yue watched him work and drew the steps in her notebook. No spiritual sight was required. Later, when she could examine a controlled trace, the separated samples would let her ask a specific question instead of announcing that the air felt strange.

foundry_arrival_023.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_023.text: The foreman found a cracked cover over the violet storage tray. The tray was removed from the open yard, and its contents stayed out of apprentice practice. Nobody accused the last worker to pass it of damaging it without evidence. The cover's old repair had loosened under heat. Su Yan showed Yue the dry fracture surface, then the newer bright edge. Their ages differed enough to guide the repair, but not enough to name the instant of failure. Cultivation instruments did not excuse ordinary uncertainty.

foundry_arrival_024.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_024.text: That evening Yue retained slightly less reserve than at the north landing. She wanted to blame the dust. Su Yan asked how much qi she had admitted after the shutters closed. None. How much ordinary work? More than her usual day. How much sleep the night before? Less, because she had listened to the floorboards. The dust remained a hazard requiring inspection; it did not explain every disappointing number. Yue ate another half bowl and entered both the travel fatigue and the unproved possibility.

foundry_arrival_025.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_025.text: After supper, she walked to the bridge without opening her field. The cooling water below carried grey sediment toward covered basins. Nothing here resembled the shining stairs she had imagined as a girl. Yet every bench held a place where one measured change could become another. She leaned on the ordinary parapet and let the longing hurt without turning it into a demand on her body. When the evening bell sounded, she returned to the room and slept before planning a breakthrough.

foundry_arrival_026.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_026.text: On the third morning, the baseline returned within her previous range. The first arm pair carried its tested quarter-unit task and released cleanly. Su Yan checked the next-day sensation before countersigning the local baseline. Yue expected the next page to name the fourth stage. It named material compatibility instead. The examiner slid over a ceramic comb with six separate contact teeth. 'You cannot open a second route safely if you send the wrong fraction through the first. We begin by learning what this tool can and cannot tell us.'

foundry_arrival_027.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_027.text: The comb's teeth were not a model of six opened pairs. They were six external sampling contacts, each connected to its own visible discharge path. The distinction mattered immediately. Yue's eye had supplied an anatomical promise to an ordinary instrument. Su Yan made her cover the comb and draw its wires from memory. Two lines crossed on Yue's first drawing where they did not cross on the bench. She erased them. A beautiful diagram could smuggle an imagined connection into the body that trusted it.

foundry_arrival_028.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_028.text: The phase comb belonged to the workshop and stayed there. Yue signed for supervised use, not possession. Its repair history included one replaced tooth and a lifted glaze seam beneath the fourth contact. Those imperfections did not make it useless; they made a blank comparison essential. Zhen fetched the old unpowered copper strip. The apparently humbler tool would check the expensive one. Yue set them side by side, grateful that learning this did not require buying either.

foundry_arrival_029.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_029.text: Su Yan drew the first month's timetable with long spaces between its ambitious words. Ordinary shifts alternated with small sampling sessions; no new internal route would open during the first fortnight. The six-week place might end with better diagnosis and no advancement. Yue asked whether that counted as failing. 'It may disappoint you,' Su Yan said. 'That is different from leaving your hand worse than you brought it.' Yue folded the timetable carefully. She would need to read that distinction more than once.

foundry_arrival_030.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_030.text: Before the morning shift, Yue wrote a letter to Duan Zhi. She described the dry baseline, her missed blank and the temptation of the split lamp. She did not turn the admission into a victory speech. At the bottom she asked whether the old caliper's repaired salt bridge had held through the wet season. The letter connected two workshops without carrying anyone's private copy or commissioning a reply without postage. She paid the ordinary courier fee from her wages and kept the food account whole.

foundry_arrival_031.speaker: narrator
foundry_arrival_031.text: By the end of her first foundry week, Yue knew the quickest path between the ash bins and the wash station. She knew which floorboard knocked, which shelf cooled unevenly and how to close her field before a dust gust. She remained at Qi Gathering's third stage. That sentence bothered her less when followed by everything she could now explain. The second-pair page was still empty. The pages before it had begun to acquire a foundation made of facts rather than eagerness.

foundry_end_bench.speaker: narrator
foundry_end_bench.text: The next six-week term began beneath the same ash bridge. Yue's two tested pairs issued small commands while separate stone charges warmed the chamber. She checked every return and wrote the actual losses beside the useful tasks. At supper, the old work tablet lay next to the fourth-stage cord. No fifth-stage mark had appeared overnight. The open space beyond the second pair remained a future she could work toward. For now, the bench held an earned skill, an honest limit and enough rice to begin another day.
foundry_end_bench.ending: Two Routes at the Work Bench

foundry_phase_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_001.text: The first phase lesson began with five uncharged powders and a sixth empty well. Su Yan called their workshop names: green wood ash, red kiln salt, yellow earth fines, white metal bloom and black water glass. The names described repeatable behavior in this method, not the moral character of a substance. A dark powder was not inherently corrupt. A bright one was not safe. Yue drew five columns, then a wider column for things a surface color could not establish.

foundry_phase_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_002.text: Each well had its own external contact and return. A reference stone supplied the comb's comparison pulse; none of that test charge entered Yue's body. She operated the shutter only after tracing the physical discharge paths again. The wood-ash fraction delayed the reference. The kiln salt brightened sooner. Su Yan asked her to repeat them with their covers exchanged. Yue discovered that the glowing label in her imagination had been contributing to a reading the instrument had never given.

foundry_phase_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_003.text: On a slate beside the tool, the examiner wrote input, recovered output and lost charge. One unit admitted to a test plate returned three quarters through its measuring path. The missing quarter had warmed the plate and dispersed into the grounding pot. It had not vanished from the energy account, nor remained available to refill another vessel. Yue touched the plate only after discharge. Its ordinary warmth made the loss easier to believe than the neat numbers alone.

foundry_phase_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_004.text: The comb did not say which fraction belonged in her route. It compared a material's response to the workshop reference. Su Yan would need Yue's prior root classification, a compatible personal sample and separate checks before interpreting that comparison. The tool's sixth blank mattered as much as its five colored wells. If the blank answered, the plate itself or the surrounding field was contributing a signal. Yue rubbed away the little arrow she had drawn from the green result straight into her dantian.

foundry_phase_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_005.text: Zhen asked whether a five-phase root required equal amounts of every fraction. Su Yan set five unequal pebbles on the slate. 'Classification tells us which conversions can appear. It does not establish their efficiency in this body on this day.' Some mixed roots tolerated broad blends with little output; some tolerated a narrow blend well and changed slowly. Yue's ordinary root remained ordinary. No hidden sixth phase waited to rescue its low efficiency from the need for more work.

foundry_phase_006.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_006.text: Her first personal sample used an eighth-unit drawn through the already tested pair. The sampling loss came out of her reserve, although the reference lamps drew from the stone. Yue kept both entries. Under the comb, her sample answered most cleanly to the earth and metal references, less efficiently to the others. Su Yan refused to turn one morning into a permanent constitution. The next comparisons would follow normal work, sleep and independent calibration, exactly because a flattering first pattern was so easy to adopt.

foundry_phase_007.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_007.text: Yue asked whether she should abandon the weaker phases. The examiner pointed to the first pair's return trace. Its timing stayed smoother when a small water-compatible fraction was present, even though that fraction converted poorly into stored reserve. Useful balance could cost efficiency. The least productive component might still matter to the route's recovery. Yue thought of the workers whose slow inspection let the quick furnace crew fire safely. The analogy helped her remember the distinction; it did not prove the physiology.

foundry_phase_008.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_008.text: They ended the personal session with the reserve above its declared floor. Su Yan checked the cuff's discharge and made Yue wash her hands before ordinary sorting. The comb remained on its bench. Carrying its result away did not mean carrying its power away. Yue could already imagine presenting herself as someone whose five phases had been measured. She wrote the actual claim instead: one recovered personal sample, observed under one calibrated comparison, awaiting repetition.

foundry_phase_009.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_009.text: During the afternoon shift, she found two batches of metal bloom stored together. Their ordinary weights and colors matched. One had cooled in a long thin sheet; the other in a thick cup. The thicker sample retained heat longer and gave a delayed external response after the same reference pulse. The material name alone did not fix its behavior. Processing history could preserve a difference no root classification would erase. Yue separated the trays and asked the foreman to confirm their batch marks.

foundry_phase_010.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_010.text: The foreman knew the marks but had not seen a reason to keep the cooled shapes apart. Su Yan demonstrated the different discharge tails on two isolated pads. Both batches could serve ordinary glaze work; only the thin sheet was currently rated for apprentice sampling. The rejected cup material was not poison in every use. Its slower return was a specific problem near a novice interruption limit. Yue entered that precise limit rather than giving the whole tray a dramatic name.

foundry_phase_011.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_011.text: At her room's table, Yue copied the long discharge curve beside her own first-pair limit. A pulse might fit the route's quantity allowance yet linger beyond its safe duration. She had understood that abstractly at the sluice. Here she could see a cup continuing to answer after its inlet closed. The future second pair would introduce another return time. Reserve, phase compatibility, rate and duration were four questions; a single larger number could not answer all of them.

foundry_phase_012.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_012.text: The next morning the blank well lit faintly. Yue felt a familiar jolt: another instrument fault, and another chance to prove she had learned. She almost announced a hidden bridge. Instead she closed the shutter, grounded the board and waited for Su Yan. The examiner found a thin condensation film beneath the replaced tooth. The repair history had suggested where to look, but only the inspection identified the present cause. Memory narrowed a search; it did not turn a suspicion into a measurement.

foundry_phase_013.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_013.text: Zhen cleaned the well with an unpowered brush while Yue inspected the return strip. The faulty comparison was discarded, not averaged with the good one to make the numbers look stable. Cleaning consumed part of the morning's teaching time. Nobody recovered those minutes by doubling the next personal dose. Su Yan demonstrated the repaired blank, then postponed Yue's sample until the next recovered session. A scheduling loss was ordinary. A damaged route would be a different kind of loss.

foundry_phase_014.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_014.text: Yue spent the unexpected free hour copying the comb's limitations in plain words. It could compare charge response at its contacts. It could not look through tissue, read intention, identify a soul or certify an unopened meridian by resemblance. The highest-stage examiner in the room still used touch reports, ordinary pulse, rest and next-day checks. Yue found that comforting only after she stopped wanting the instrument to remove uncertainty on her behalf.

foundry_phase_015.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_015.text: On the fourth recovered comparison, her personal fractions stayed within the same practical range. Su Yan approved a narrow compatible blend for future low-dose practice, with a water component retained for smooth return. The approval named the actual batches and their inspected cooling form. Buying another material with the same trade name would require comparison. Yue copied the batch marks carefully. Poverty made her want a cheap substitute; wanting did not make its discharge tail fit her hand.

foundry_phase_016.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_016.text: The blend improved usable retention by less than a unit. It did not triple her reserve or change the stage written beside her name. Yue still felt delighted. A small repeatable gain was more real than the impossible gain she had hoped for when first touching the violet wafer. She placed the successful comparison next to the missed blank from her first day. The improvement belonged to the sequence that included the mistake, rather than to a revised story in which she had always understood.

foundry_phase_017.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_017.text: A letter from Duan Zhi arrived with ash caught beneath its fold. The repaired caliper remained sound, he wrote, but the wet season had required new grounding checks. He asked whether Yue was still eating before late practice. There was no extraordinary manual enclosed, only an ordinary question whose answer affected the next day's numbers. Yue read the letter twice and moved her meal bowl away from the notebook. She would finish supper before writing a reply about the difficult parts.

foundry_phase_018.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_018.text: Her reply admitted that she had wanted the violet material because it looked like cultivation ought to look. Duan's teaching had survived the journey; her vanity had traveled with it. She described the prolonged discharge in thick cups and asked whether comparable tails appeared in the sluice's stored relay charge. The question might help both workshops later. It did not require an answer before her next test, and she wrote that explicitly so her curiosity would not become someone else's urgent unpaid work.

foundry_phase_019.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_019.text: Su Yan invited her to observe a senior's fourth-stage comparison from behind the isolation line. The student routed two small pulses successively, not together, with a full discharge between them. Each internal pair had its own allowed delay. At the common shoulder junction, the second route's return slightly disturbed the first. The disturbance remained under that student's tested limit. Yue watched without imitating the movement inside her own body. Seeing a successful route did not supply the tissue preparation it required.

foundry_phase_020.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_020.text: The senior admitted that his first fourth-stage trial had failed after an ordinary heavy shift. His second pair had returned cleanly in quiet practice and poorly under fatigue. He had reduced his work temporarily rather than declaring the stage won by the better day. Yue had assumed higher students were past such repetitions. The admission made their lamps less distant. She would still need her own examinations, but she no longer pictured advancement as entering a place where facts stopped being inconvenient.

foundry_phase_021.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_021.text: Su Yan outlined the foundry's fourth-stage assessment: eighteen usable units after ordinary activity and sleep, at least eighty-seven percent compatible charge, two distinct paired routes each carrying its permitted quarter-unit task, reliable interruption and no abnormal next-day sensation. The paths would be tested successively before any combined practice was considered. These were local method thresholds, not universal coin values. Yue wrote the reserve figure last. The route conditions were harder to imagine and therefore easier to neglect.

foundry_phase_022.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_022.text: The second pair followed the complementary outer-forearm and upper-arm paths to the shoulder junction. It did not open a leg channel, the middle dantian or an extraordinary vessel. Su Yan marked the permitted region on an unpowered chart, leaving later routes covered. Yue recognized the old temptation to treat the next visible line as permission. This time she placed a folded cloth over it herself. She would learn the second return before dreaming of a circuit large enough to make every part of the drawing useful.

foundry_phase_023.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_023.text: Preparation would begin with ordinary shoulder alignment, then external reference work, then tiny supervised route admissions after recovered examinations. No internal second-pair pulse was scheduled yet. Yue asked how long it took. Su Yan answered with a range and the reason she would not promise a date: tissue response, ordinary workload, material compatibility and the first pair's continued condition could change the pace. The six-week bench place might become twelve weeks. Yue counted the return fare again before deciding she could stay for the first term.

foundry_phase_024.speaker: narrator
foundry_phase_024.text: That night she reached the bridge as the last furnace shutter closed. Below, a cooling cup answered its residual charge with one faint violet fleck. Yue watched it fade without taking that persistence for strength. The same lingering tail might hold a useful material memory or hurt an unprepared return route. Cultivation was becoming detailed enough to resist her favorite metaphors. She could still love the light. She also needed to know when it would stop.

foundry_craft_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_001.text: In the third week, the foreman assigned Yue to annealing cups rather than ash baskets. She learned to distinguish a glaze crack from a body crack by ordinary light and a soft wooden tap. Neither test was conclusive alone. The teaching cup carried both kinds. Yue liked that it defeated a quick answer. Her first arm pair remained closed during the inspection; opening it would add a warmth she could mistake for a property of the vessel.

foundry_craft_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_002.text: The ordinary clay body expanded under heat more slowly than the violet coating. On cooling, the difference pulled fine seams through the glaze. A careful firing schedule could reduce those stresses. It could not make incompatible expansion rates identical. Yue held a cross-section against the window and saw why the thick test cups had retained charged islands. The islands were small enough to look harmless and persistent enough to outlast an apprentice's expected discharge.

foundry_craft_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_003.text: Su Yan separated two uses of the seam. A rated storage cup might deliberately hold a known charge behind it. A sampling plate needed prompt release and could fail for the same reason that made the cup useful. The foundry had treated a batch name as permission to substitute one use for the other. Yue copied the two specifications on separate pages. Craft knowledge had become a way to prevent a cultivation injury before any qi entered her field.

foundry_craft_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_004.text: She spent a morning scraping unfired clay for reusable material. The work had no spiritual drama, but it made the cost of a spoiled firing visible. Charcoal, clay, labor and furnace time would not return merely because the finished cups could not serve their intended role. Some could become ordinary storage; some required breaking down. Yue sorted them by demonstrated use. Calling every rejected cup a catastrophe would waste resources as surely as calling each one acceptable.

foundry_craft_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_005.text: At the paid bench, Zhen showed her a little glazed disc he had made after work. Its pattern curved like an opened channel. Yue admired it before asking whether it was a practice device. It was a spoon rest. He laughed and set his sticky brush on it. She laughed too, with more relief than the joke deserved. Not every beautiful object in a cultivation workshop needed to promise another realm.

foundry_craft_006.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_006.text: A visiting merchant offered the apprentices a powder said to shorten every route-opening period. He brought a genuine ordinary assay for its grain size and no recovered route trials. Su Yan let him speak, then asked for the missing measurements. The merchant described the confidence of his repeat customers. Yue watched his smooth answer fill the space where a discharge tail should have been. She kept her copper in its pouch.

foundry_craft_007.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_007.text: One older apprentice bought a small packet for ordinary glaze work, where its grain size was useful and the risks differed. Su Yan did not accuse him of poisoning himself. He marked the packet's allowed use and kept it out of the route cupboard. Yue found the distinction harder than a blanket ban. It asked her to understand a purpose rather than obey an object's reputation. She copied the allowed use with her own name absent from the purchaser line.

foundry_craft_008.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_008.text: On the bridge that afternoon, she remembered the childhood kiln where she had spoiled rice by placing it near a hot vent. The embarrassment had taught her about heat long before any trace remained in her body. The foundry did not retroactively make that childhood a cultivation miracle. It gave the old ordinary lesson a new place: useful energy still needed the right path, duration and distance from what it could damage.

foundry_craft_009.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_009.text: Her mother had stretched money by repairing vessels whose cracks could still be kept dry. Yue wrote to her about the foundry's rejected cups and the meal account. She did not say that an ordinary childhood had secretly prepared a superior root. She said that the work she once despised had left her better able to notice a seam. The letter included a small remittance from completed wages, after food and return fare, rather than money borrowed against an expected breakthrough.

foundry_craft_010.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_010.text: The third-week examination began with ordinary shoulder movement. Yue lifted an unpowered wooden ring, turned it slowly and reported where the old carry habit tightened. Su Yan marked the right shoulder's inward turn without naming it a spiritual blockage. First they adjusted the grip and ordinary posture. If a muscle carried the error, adding qi might reinforce it. Yue practiced with the ring until the movement no longer required a spiritual explanation.

foundry_craft_011.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_011.text: The ring was deliberately plain. Its only virtue was a weight the examiner could reproduce. Yue borrowed it for twenty minutes, returned it, and performed the same movement empty-handed. The easier sensation without weight did not erase the loaded limit. After the check, she sorted cups at a low table so the ordinary shift would not repeat the tiring overhead motion. Work and training still shared one body even when their accounts were separate.

foundry_craft_012.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_012.text: Su Yan used an external strip to demonstrate the second pair's return timing. The current came from the reference socket and remained outside Yue's tissue. Two paths reached the same visible junction at different intervals. When the examiner overlapped them, one return intruded into the other. She stopped the test and discharged both. A first clean route did not guarantee the junction could distinguish a second one merely because each path looked clean by itself.

foundry_craft_013.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_013.text: Yue asked why they would open another pair if the first worked. Su Yan placed two ordinary tasks beside the slate: a control held briefly at the chestward path and a separate forearm return needed while repositioning the hand. One pair required discharge between them. A second tested pair could eventually offer a different route and better distribution within limits. It would not double every ability. Yue liked the answer less than an astonishing promise, and trusted it more.

foundry_craft_014.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_014.text: At home that evening, she tried to draw the junction without joining the routes prematurely. Twice her stylus made a continuous circle where the current procedure required a visible stop. She erased the circle and left an empty gap. The great heavenly circuit existed in the manual, many stages ahead. The blank space on her little drawing was not a flaw to beautify. It recorded the part of cultivation she had not earned.

foundry_craft_015.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_015.text: After an ordinary shift, her shoulder remained sore from the ring exercise. Su Yan canceled the planned external reference session even though its current would not enter Yue. Watching it tired her attention and tempted her to rehearse the route internally. Yue protested that she could simply promise not to do that. The examiner asked her to name when she had last mistaken a neighboring lamp for a distraction she could control. Yue put the cuff away.

foundry_craft_016.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_016.text: Zhen offered to finish the shelf labels while she rested the shoulder. Yue offered to mend his torn sleeve later, without turning either favor into a lifetime obligation. Their exchange was small enough to finish. She realized she was less comfortable accepting the first favor than offering the second. Years of being an applicant had made help seem like evidence that she did not belong. The sleeve on her lap proved only that work could move between people.

foundry_craft_017.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_017.text: Two days later, the ordinary check returned to baseline. No new meridian had opened during the rest. The saved practice fuel remained in the workshop's finite allowance; it did not automatically entitle her to a doubled session. She used a small reference comparison, then stopped. The shoulder's recovery pleased her more quietly than a bright pulse would have. It also left her able to complete the paid work that funded another week at the bench.

foundry_craft_018.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_018.text: Near the end of the third week, the foreman offered three ways to schedule the next stretch. Yue could take modest cup-sorting shifts, spend more teaching time on batch records, or keep a lighter rota while repeating the ordinary shoulder work. Each maintained meals and the same minimum supervised examinations. Their extra opportunities differed. Su Yan would not award a realm for a work choice, and the foreman would not make food depend on choosing the hardest shift.

foundry_craft_019.speaker: narrator
foundry_craft_019.text: Yue laid her examination notebook beside the rota before answering. The first-pair reserve remained stable. The shoulder was newly recovered. The disputed violet batch still lacked a clear processing history. She could help most by understanding one of those facts better, but she could not pursue every option at once and sleep normally. The choices were ordinary enough to make the temptation sharper: no dramatic sacrifice would hide which limit she had decided to respect.

foundry_work_choice.speaker: lin_yue
foundry_work_choice.text: The next rota leaves room for one extra emphasis. I can earn the modest sorting wage, compare the disputed batch's cooling records, or keep the lighter schedule while repeating the recovered shoulder exercises. Each keeps meals, ordinary sleep and the required supervised tests. I cannot make a second pair by choosing the most impressive label. I can choose what work gives the next examination a sounder starting point.

choices.text: Compare the disputed batch's cooling history.
Keep the lighter rota and recovered shoulder practice.

foundry_wage_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_wage_001.text: Yue chose the modest sorting shift and began with the cups whose intended use had been crossed out. She checked each against the ordinary glaze specifications rather than the apprentice sampling standard. Reassigning a sound cup saved work without pretending it was suitable for every circuit. By noon she had recovered a tray for dry storage and rejected two cups with body cracks. Her hands remained ordinary; the extra wage was credited only after the foreman checked the finished tray.

foundry_wage_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_wage_002.text: The wage looked small beside the cost of a packet of rated practice mineral. Yue divided it anyway: a little for replacement cloth, a little held against a delayed return, nothing committed to a promised future breakthrough. She still wanted better materials. The completed tray gave her money she could actually spend, unlike the value she imagined a fourth-stage name would bring. She entered the earning beside the extra ordinary load so the next examination could interpret both.

foundry_wage_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_wage_003.text: On the last sorting afternoon she found a thick cup with a smooth glaze seam hidden beneath its foot. It remained acceptable for uncharged dry storage and suspect for rapid discharge. Yue attached the specific use limit before putting it on the recovered shelf. She had not discovered the whole disputed batch history. She had learned to apply the existing distinction consistently, a skill that mattered when an attractive vessel tempted her to forget its underside.

foundry_wage_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_wage_004.text: Zhen checked her recovered tray independently and disagreed about one cup near the margin. They compared it with the teaching specimen, then asked the foreman. The cup moved to a restricted shelf pending another inspection. Neither apprentice lost the completed wages for reporting the uncertainty. Yue felt the old urge to defend every decision as proof of competence. Instead she made the uncertainty visible and finished the task within the promised shift.

foundry_wage_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_wage_005.text: The following morning she brought the wage entry and workload record to Su Yan. The examiner treated the extra labor as a condition to inspect, not a virtue that earned more qi. Yue's sleeping reserve stayed within its recent range. Her ordinary shoulder check stayed normal. The rota had bought supplies and practiced a useful judgment; it had not purchased the second pair.

foundry_records_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_records_001.text: Yue chose the batch records and sat beneath a shelf where firing slates cooled in the shade. She compared the disputed violet material's thick-cup schedule with the thin-sheet schedule, keeping their sources separate. The cup had received an extra cooling hold intended to preserve small charged islands for storage. That hold had later disappeared from a copied summary. The missing instruction explained a plausible difference in discharge; it did not establish who had omitted it or why.

foundry_records_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_records_002.text: She marked the copying gap and fetched the original firing slate with the keeper's permission. Its old glaze splash obscured one time mark. Yue resisted filling the mark from the neighboring entries. She made a literal copy of the visible parts and left the interval bounded by what could be read. The cup's behavior could be tested without inventing a precise historical minute. The keeper signed the limited extract, retaining the original in its own shelf.

foundry_records_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_records_003.text: Su Yan compared the extract with two isolated sample pads, one cut from a thick cup and one from a thin sheet. The longer tail remained consistent with the extra hold, though shape and thickness also differed. Yue wrote that the comparison had not isolated every variable. The report still supported keeping the cup material out of novice route sampling. An action could be justified by a demonstrated limit before every cause had been settled.

foundry_records_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_records_004.text: The foreman offered to put Yue's name at the top of the corrected specification. Yue asked that the keeper, examiner and ordinary cooling crew remain visible too. She had traced the copy gap; others had preserved and tested the sources. Refusing sole credit did not make her work vanish. Her contribution stayed specific enough for the next worker to repeat it without needing to believe a story about one unusually perceptive apprentice.

foundry_records_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_records_005.text: At the morning examination she laid the limited extract beside her sleep and workload record. Hours at the copying table had spared her shoulder but tired her eyes. Su Yan shortened the visual comparison and kept the ordinary sensation check. Better evidence about the batch did not make Yue's own body more rested. She had gained a sharper question, not an automatic stage.

foundry_rest_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_rest_001.text: Yue chose the lighter rota and carried the wooden ring to a shaded practice space. The ordinary shoulder movement felt easy until she tried to rush its return. Then the old inward twist reappeared. She reduced the speed rather than adding a trace to make the movement feel stronger. No examiner would call the empty-handed rehearsal a meridian opening. It prepared a body that would later need to distinguish ordinary strain from a new route's warning.

foundry_rest_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_rest_002.text: During the saved evening hour, she slept before the apprentice room grew quiet. Missing the senior lamp demonstration felt like missing an opportunity. By morning her hands were steady and the first-pair comparison required less compensating attention. Yue recorded the actual result without claiming that rest must improve every number. This time it had removed one known burden. That was enough reason to preserve it in the next week's plan.

foundry_rest_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_rest_003.text: Zhen asked whether she regretted the smaller wage. Yue counted the supplies already covered by the ordinary account and admitted that a new cuff would have been welcome. The choice had a cost even when it was sensible. They mended the existing cuff after the wash station dried it. A patched item could serve its rated use; the patch would need inspection. Rest had not produced a better artifact from nothing.

foundry_rest_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_rest_004.text: On the fourth practice morning, Su Yan watched the ring movement under its ordinary load. The shoulder stayed aligned through the slow turn and return. Yue repeated it without weight, then stopped before fatigue changed the pattern. The examiner permitted a later external reference session, with the same dose limit as before. The improvement widened the conditions she could meet. It did not waive the next gate.

foundry_rest_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_rest_005.text: Yue brought the lighter rota's record to the common review. She had neither earned the extra sorting copper nor personally traced the batch's copied cooling hold. She had a recovered shoulder pattern and clearer ordinary limits to offer. Su Yan kept those facts distinct. Yue was learning to bring useful work to a table without needing every other person's useful work to become part of her own history.

foundry_work_rejoin_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_work_rejoin_001.text: At the common bench, Su Yan presented the batch report and the foreman's corrected use limits to every apprentice. The keeper's original slate remained on its shelf; the permitted extract traveled no farther than the workshop review. Whatever rota Yue had chosen, she now knew the cup material's demonstrated long discharge tail. The report credited the actual workers rather than assuming she had followed a records route. No future route would depend on an inquiry she might never have made.

foundry_work_rejoin_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_work_rejoin_002.text: The shared review kept the three rotas' costs visible. Sorting had paid copper and added ordinary load. Copying had clarified a source while tiring attention. A lighter schedule had supported recovery while forgoing extra earnings. All three preserved meals, the first pair's checks and supervised access. Su Yan did not turn the comparison into a contest in moral worth. Cultivation would still have to pass the same physical examinations after any of them.

foundry_work_rejoin_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_work_rejoin_003.text: Now the examiner laid out the second-pair preparation chart. Its first line required Yue's current shoulder baseline and her first pair's clean interruption. Its last line named recovered trials she had not yet reached. The middle contained small steps with room to retreat. Yue recognized the chart's empty spaces as part of its usefulness. They kept an ambitious schedule from pretending the next result was already known.

foundry_work_rejoin_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_work_rejoin_004.text: She set the phase comb's blank beside a rated thin-sheet sample. The new material blend would be compared externally before any supervised admission. This time she looked at the empty well first. A result that appeared there would stop the session, however promising the five colored contacts looked. She could still hear the senior lamps from the adjoining bay. Their light no longer decided which part of her own bench deserved attention.

foundry_route_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_001.text: At the first supervised preparation session, Su Yan laid two unpowered strips along the chart's allowed region. Yue named the first pair's existing return, then the second pair's proposed shoulder junction. She had to distinguish them without following either internally. The examiner varied the chart's orientation. Yue made one mistake when the shoulder mark faced away from her. They corrected the naming before admitting a trace. Confusing a drawing was cheap; rehearsing its mistake through tissue would not be.

foundry_route_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_002.text: The ordinary shoulder movement remained sound that morning and after the sorting shift. Only then did the examiner permit a tiny first admission toward the complementary forearm path. Yue used one sixteenth of a unit, far below the eventual quarter-unit test. The new sensation was broad and uncertain, more like pressure near the skin than the clean turn of the established pair. She described it without pretending to have found the whole line shown on the chart.

foundry_route_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_003.text: Su Yan stopped the session at that description. An uncertain sensation could be recorded and revisited after rest. It could not be pushed into agreement with a remembered map. The first pair discharged normally; the proposed route had not carried a tested return. Yue kept the stage-three label. That night, ordinary touch remained normal. She wanted to announce the start of a second pair in her letter home, then chose the smaller claim she could defend.

foundry_route_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_004.text: Two recovered mornings later, the same tiny admission followed a more distinct forearm line. Su Yan checked the blank reference and asked Yue to interrupt before reaching the shoulder. She closed the admission and felt the pressure recede slowly. Slow was not automatically abnormal; they compared it with the allowed trial interval. The result justified repeating the same small dose after recovery. It did not justify doubling it while enthusiasm made the return feel easier.

foundry_route_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_005.text: For eight days the new work advanced in fractions too small to look heroic. A clean morning could be followed by an ordinary day that tired the shoulder. A fresh material pad needed its own external comparison. Each delay threatened Yue's imagined schedule, though none violated the actual one. Zhen began saying 'another permitted attempt' when she said 'another lost day.' The phrase annoyed her until she heard how often her own language made the body seem disobedient.

foundry_route_006.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_006.text: During a rain-cooled afternoon, the forearm admission reached its provisional shoulder limit without tightness. Yue could identify the way back and release before the examiner's cue ended. The outward partner remained unfinished. A one-way sensation did not make a pair. Su Yan covered the next section of the chart and assigned ordinary work for the following day. Yue was allowed to be pleased; she was not allowed to spend that pleasure as additional throughput.

foundry_route_007.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_007.text: The provisional return began beside the upper arm, joining the shoulder region by a separate cultivated path. Su Yan emphasized that these routes described controlled associations with living tissue, not physical holes waiting to be pierced. Yue watched the slate's line while keeping her own attention on a much less beautiful sensation. The diagram had clean borders. Her body offered gradients, uncertainty and fatigue. The practice needed repeatable control through those facts rather than a perfect internal picture.

foundry_route_008.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_008.text: At the end of the fourth week, she could repeat a small admission and an incomplete return under quiet conditions. Her reserve had grown gradually with the compatible blend, but remained below the fourth-stage sleeping target on working days. The record held two kinds of unfinished progress. Yue found the route's promise more exciting than the reserve column and kept wanting to substitute it. Su Yan asked her to read both aloud before planning the next session.

foundry_route_009.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_009.text: A furnace repair changed the air around the teaching bay. The temperature rose by only a few ordinary degrees, within the building's general working limit. Yue's practice pad had cooled on a shelf closer to the reopened flue. Its external blank looked normal in the shade. Nobody yet knew that the permitted material's return tail lengthened when warmed against a working cuff. The safe batch name concealed a condition their previous comparisons had not reproduced.

foundry_route_010.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_010.text: The fifth-week trial began with the first pair's standard check. Yue reported no abnormal sensation, and the reference comparisons passed at room temperature. Su Yan permitted the familiar small second-route dose. Near the shoulder junction, the return faded more slowly than it had on the cool afternoons. Yue noticed it. She also noticed how close the visible chart lay to the point she wanted to reach. For one breath she waited instead of calling the delay.

foundry_route_011.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_011.text: Then the pressure sharpened. Yue closed the admission and said 'late return' before trying another pulse. Su Yan isolated the external pad, kept the first pair's ordinary discharge available and ended the work. No one sent a larger qi wave into her shoulder to force the unfinished path clear. Yue sat with both feet on the floor and described the sensation until it stopped changing. The blank on the bench remained quiet, which made the failure more frightening rather than less.

foundry_route_012.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_012.text: The wash-room healer examined ordinary touch, grip and pulse without asking Yue to reproduce the event. Two fingers felt dull for part of the afternoon, then recovered ordinary sensation. The shoulder remained tender. Su Yan wrote an immediate rest order for new-route work and suspended powered use of the cuff pending material tests. The first pair's earned stage remained in the record; its current safe use had to be inspected again. A certificate was not permission to ignore a changed body.

foundry_route_013.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_013.text: Yue wanted to say the pad alone had caused it. She also wanted to blame herself entirely and turn punishment into certainty. The examiner accepted neither shortcut. They knew the late return, the warmed cuff and Yue's brief delay in reporting. They did not yet know how those factors interacted. Her silence had shortened the time available to stop. It had not established every material cause. Yue entered both the personal lapse and the unresolved technical question.

foundry_route_014.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_014.text: That night she lay awake with her hand outside the blanket. Every ordinary tingle seemed like the beginning of a permanent loss. Zhen offered to fetch the healer if anything changed, then left the lamp where Yue could reach it. He did not insist that optimism would make the route recover. Yue finally slept when she stopped examining the fingers every minute. The next morning's sensation was ordinary; the next practice page stayed closed.

foundry_route_015.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_015.text: Su Yan tested the suspect pad through an external rig, using workshop fuel and no apprentice route. At its cool baseline, the tail fitted the old limit. At ordinary cuff temperature, it persisted longer. The same delayed tail appeared in a fresh piece from the batch. The instrument's blank remained clean. This was not the old salt bridge returning in a different story. A material property changed with heat, and their permitted comparison had missed that condition.

foundry_route_016.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_016.text: The examiner laid the warm and cool curves beside Yue's recorded delay. The match supported removing that pad from personal route use. It did not prove the precise cause of every tender sensation in the shoulder. The healer's examination and recovery still mattered. Yue watched the two curves without feeling absolved into carelessness. She would report a changed return immediately next time, including one that appeared while all familiar blanks looked reassuring.

foundry_route_017.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_017.text: The foreman closed the affected personal-practice tray and kept its material available only for rated storage uses. The workshop paid for the revised external tests and inspection. Yue's ordinary wages continued for light work she could perform; the paid place did not become a debt because the training had failed. She would lose time and confidence. The policy prevented those losses from being joined by hunger, which would have made both the record and the recovery harder.

foundry_route_018.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_018.text: The new-route rest order lasted fourteen days before reassessment, with extension if ordinary checks failed. It was not a promise that fourteen days would heal every injury. Yue could retain a small quiet field only within the healer's revised limits, and the cuff stayed out of use. She could read, mend cloth and perform low-load sorting. She could not secretly rehearse the second pair because the pathway felt easier after a warm compress.

foundry_route_019.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_019.text: Su Yan visited the room with a plain bowl of soup. Yue expected another chart. 'Charts tomorrow,' the examiner said. She had once damaged her own route by trying to finish a furnace shift after its return timing changed. The scar at her jaw came from the ordinary hot shell she dropped afterward, not from a glorious tribulation. Her ninth stage did not mean she had always been wise. It meant that the surviving lessons were part of her present inspection practice.

foundry_route_020.speaker: narrator
foundry_route_020.text: Yue asked whether wanting cultivation so much made her unsafe. Su Yan considered the question before answering. 'Wanting is why you stay to learn. It also changes which facts you are tempted to edit. We train the editing habit alongside the route.' The soup cooled between them. Yue finished it before asking about the revised pad. There would be time to understand the fault if she did not use understanding as an excuse to stop caring for the body that had felt it.

foundry_recovery_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_001.text: The failure entry named Day Thirty-one. Yue wrote the date beside the fourteen-day reassessment interval, then put the examination cord in her drawer. Naming the day did not make the wait shorter. It did prevent her fear from stretching it into an indistinct exile. The ordinary healer's instructions remained separate from Su Yan's material inquiry. Neither would be replaced by how calm Yue managed to appear at breakfast.

foundry_recovery_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_002.text: For the first three days, she performed no powered cuff work. A quiet lower field stayed within the healer's reduced retention limit; it was not circulated into the resting shoulder. Her old twelve-unit performance remained a past examination result. Present practice had smaller permission. Yue had once imagined that gaining a stage meant keeping every part of its use forever. The foundry was teaching her to preserve an earned capacity by admitting when its use had changed.

foundry_recovery_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_003.text: She took light work counting uncharged lids at a low table. The task paid less than handling full trays and did not load the shoulder. Zhen brought the lids down; Yue marked the completed count and returned them by small stacks. The arrangement had an actual end at the healer's next review. She did not promise to repay help through an indefinite future duty. Zhen wanted accurate lids today, not a claim over her eventual cultivation.

foundry_recovery_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_004.text: The room's senior student came to see her with the split-lamp tube she had once watched so hungrily. He left its socket empty. The instrument could be examined as ordinary craft while she rested, but she asked him to keep it in his own drawer. She knew how readily looking became internal rehearsal when she wanted a route badly enough. Declining the object did not require pretending she no longer wanted to learn its circuit.

foundry_recovery_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_005.text: On the fifth rest day, the shoulder felt almost ordinary. Yue caught herself planning a hidden tiny pulse to find out whether it truly was. She wrote the plan down and took it to the healer instead. He examined ordinary movement and found a mild tenderness under the loaded turn. The symptom had not disappeared simply because she had ceased noticing it in bed. No powered test was added. Yue returned to the lid table angry with the answer and glad she had asked.

foundry_recovery_006.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_006.text: At supper, Zhen talked about his own stage-two retention failures. He had once improved the evening reading by skipping the work that paid his room, then presented it as a normal-day result. The lie had required more lies about meals and attendance. He withdrew the record before any advancement examination. Yue listened without making his error an excuse for her delayed warning. Their failures resembled each other enough to discuss and differed enough to need their own repairs.

foundry_recovery_007.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_007.text: The weekly wage arrived with no unexplained training deduction. Yue compared the food, light-work pay and courier expense before sending another small letter home. This one said that practice had paused and ordinary sensation was improving. She did not tell her mother that she would certainly advance by the next letter. Her mother's last reply had described a repaired roof tile and an expensive sack of grain. Those ordinary costs deserved money she could count rather than confidence she could perform.

foundry_recovery_008.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_008.text: During the seventh rest day, Su Yan showed the revised external test: cool pad, warmed pad, active sample and blank. The warming reproduced ordinary cuff temperature, not an extreme furnace condition. A material suitable only when cool could still fail in normal use. The examiner refused to blame the building's general heat limit for a missing personal-practice specification. Yue could understand the distinction while her body rested; she could not certify her own recovery from the external result.

foundry_recovery_009.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_009.text: The revised pad used a thinner compatible film with a separate physical heat sink. Its improved tail had a cost: lower useful output and more reference fuel spent in the comparison. The foreman approved that expense for apprentice safety. No one pretended the added sink created qi or that a more expensive pad must be safer. The new assembly would still need independent warm-condition blanks and personal trials after the healer cleared Yue to resume.

foundry_recovery_010.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_010.text: On Day Forty, two days before the original paid place would end, the foreman held its renewal review. She offered another six weeks from the training account, including meals, light-work options and the same separately bounded practice allowance. The revised material inquiry had its own approved budget. Yue could decline and retain her earned wages and return fare. She accepted the extension after reading the dates, not because an injury had made leaving financially impossible.

foundry_recovery_011.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_011.text: Su Yan accepted responsibility for the training specification that had missed warm-cuff testing. Yue accepted responsibility for the one-breath delay in reporting. The review entered both without forcing them to compete for a single blame. The foreman scheduled a shared inspection lesson so other apprentices would learn the revised condition. Yue's experience could help them only if its limits survived the telling. The review did not sell it as proof that pain was a shortcut to a deeper route.

foundry_recovery_012.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_012.text: Before bed, Yue opened the admission notice and replaced the old end date with Day Eighty-four on her personal schedule. She kept the next review before that date. The spare copper for a return journey remained untouched. Twelve weeks might produce a fourth stage, a safer third stage or another reason to stop. She was buying the conditions for honest practice, not the result itself.

foundry_recovery_013.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_013.text: The bridge's cooling chimneys sounded different after rain. Yue began hearing the ordinary contractions without treating every click as a warning from her body. She sat there with a bowl of ginger broth and practiced the unpowered breath she had learned as a mortal. It steadied attention; it admitted no qi and awarded no realm. Sometimes returning to the first exercise was how she kept a later stage from filling every waking minute.

foundry_recovery_014.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_014.text: By the twelfth rest day, loaded shoulder movement no longer reproduced the tenderness. The healer still kept the original reassessment date. Two good ordinary mornings did not erase the agreed observation interval. Yue counted the remaining days with less resentment than before. She had watched how quickly an anticipated date could become pressure to report the result she wanted. The interval was not sacred; the reason for retaining it was specific and legible.

foundry_recovery_015.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_015.text: On Day Forty-five, the healer repeated ordinary touch, grip and shoulder movement, including the previously tender turn. All stayed within baseline. He cleared a cautious return to the established first pair only, with a smaller dose and a next-day check. The second route remained closed to practice. Yue felt an astonishing joy at this modest permission. It returned something she already knew rather than giving her the higher stage she had arrived wanting.

foundry_recovery_016.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_016.text: Su Yan used the old reliable copper lead for the first recovered check. The revised warm-tested pad stayed off the bench. Yue admitted a small trace through the established inward path and let its return finish before speaking. It felt ordinary. The examiner recorded the completed discharge, then ended the session despite spare fuel. The next morning's normal sensation would be part of the result. Relief could tempt her to hurry just as effectively as ambition had.

foundry_recovery_017.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_017.text: The next-day examination remained normal. After a further recovered interval, Yue repeated the first pair under its old permitted conditions. Her reserve was still rebuilding toward its former working range, so no maximum task was scheduled. Returning capacity needed evidence at the load she actually held. The slate's smaller numbers no longer seemed to insult the examination cord. They told Su Yan what could be done that morning.

foundry_recovery_018.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_018.text: The third recovered first-pair check passed after a light ordinary shift. Only then did the examiner discuss using the revised pad for a future tiny admission near the second route. The new material had passed independent external tests at cool and cuff temperatures. Yue's body had passed its own limited recovery sequence. Neither set of results could stand in for the other. The next attempt would require both and preserve the same immediate stop rule.

foundry_recovery_019.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_019.text: Yue read the failure entry aloud to Zhen before the shared inspection lesson. She had written 'the material made me wait' and crossed it out. The amended sentence said she noticed a changed return and delayed reporting for one breath. The technical report named the warm tail separately. Zhen said the amended version sounded less like a hero surviving an ambush. Yue agreed. It also gave the next apprentice something specific to do differently.

foundry_recovery_020.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_020.text: The lesson used an empty cuff and an external warmed pad. Yue demonstrated the reporting words without sending a pulse through herself. The other apprentices saw the tail lengthen and the physical shutter close. The disputed material's owner allowed the specimen to remain at the teaching bench under its restricted use. A dangerous personal-practice component had become a bounded external lesson. Its new usefulness did not remove the old restriction.

foundry_recovery_021.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_021.text: At the end of the review, the foreman asked whether Yue wanted the specimen as a keepsake. She declined. Carrying it in her pack would require new precautions and invite someone later to mistake its beauty for permitted use. She kept the written comparison and the memory of the examiner's calm stop instead. Her cultivation needed less equipment than her eagerness had once insisted. It needed the right equipment, in the right place, under terms she understood.

foundry_recovery_022.speaker: narrator
foundry_recovery_022.text: The following week began with warm rain on the ash bridge. Yue returned to light cup work and scheduled small sessions around meals. The first pair remained normal; the second pair remained unfinished. Her renewed place had five weeks left, enough time to continue carefully and too little to promise the final result. Below the bridge, violet flecks appeared in a cooling seam where no practice pad had been set. That question belonged to the yard before it belonged to her route.

foundry_creature_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_001.text: The flecks beneath the bridge grew brighter after the furnace crew closed the evening shutters. Zhen called Yue to look from the dry rail, well outside the cooling seam. The glow arrived in short runs separated by darkness. At first she mistook it for a delayed material tail. Then one bright run moved against the water. A line of small hooked feet gripped the stone, carrying a plated body toward the warm waste channel.

foundry_creature_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_002.text: Its armor looked like violet glass held together by old copper rings. Tiny amber lights remained trapped inside the plates after each step. The head pressed two fine filaments against the seam and scraped with mineral jaws. Yue had seen one illustrated in the craft manual: a voidglass centipede, a spirit that fed on residual charge in cooling glaze. The illustration had not conveyed how sharp its legs sounded against stone.

foundry_creature_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_003.text: Su Yan ordered the students behind the rail and inspected the waste channel before approaching. The centipede was not a summoned trial beast. Its appearance would not be used to test Yue's bravery or earn her a route opening. It had found a real source of trapped charge in discarded material. The waste specification had allowed cool-looking fragments into a place where their remaining energy could attract a creature capable of cutting through a worker's boot.

foundry_creature_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_004.text: The creature's front segments rose toward a charged scrap cup wedged below the dry path. A porter stepped back, caught his heel on a basket and fell. Zhen pulled the basket aside while another worker helped the porter reach the stairs. Yue kept the doorway clear and counted the people entering. Nobody asked her to channel through the resting shoulder or hold the plated body with qi. Her present useful task was an ordinary one she could finish.

foundry_creature_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_005.text: Su Yan took a rated shield plate from the emergency rack. A separate charged socket fed its shallow barrier; her ninth-stage control maintained the permitted relay. The slate beside the socket showed a finite reserve and a replacement mark. Yue read it while the foreman fetched the mechanical channel shutter. Even an experienced cultivator's presence did not make the barrier an inexhaustible wall. Their plan needed to work before the stored charge reached its floor.

foundry_creature_006.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_006.text: The centipede struck the plate with one hooked leg. A violet line jumped across the barrier's face and drained through its grounded edge. The ordinary frame shook hard enough to make Yue's teeth click. Su Yan stepped within the plate's supported stance rather than chasing the beast with a blade aura. The rack and stone socket bore the sustained work. Yue saw both the formidable control and the craft that made it possible.

foundry_creature_007.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_007.text: The foreman closed the upstream scrap feed with the ordinary shutter. A grounded waste strip isolated the storage cup's remaining contact from the main channel. The beast still held charge in its own armor; source isolation did not make that disappear. Su Yan kept the barrier between it and the stairs while a second worker opened the empty downstream sluice. The creature would have to find a path through stone and cooling water, not an invitation into the apprentice benches.

foundry_creature_008.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_008.text: Behind the isolated seam, two smaller plated shapes stirred beneath a spent shell. They were young, not decorative fragments. The adults' position now made a different kind of sense, but the workshop could not assume every strike was only defense. Su Yan warned the crew to preserve distance. Understanding why an animal might attack did not make its legs safe. Yue looked for a useful place she could stand without turning sympathy into a reason to approach.

foundry_creature_009.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_009.text: A merchant at the upper rail shouted that the adult's armor would buy a better training stone than any apprentice wage. Yue felt the sentence land exactly where her impatience lived. She had no permission to hunt, no tested means to handle the charged plates and no evidence that their material belonged in her route. The emergency remained a protection task. The foreman sent the merchant away from the workers' access stairs.

foundry_creature_010.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_010.text: The shield's fuel mark fell. Su Yan called the remaining interval clearly, and the foreman chose a measured quench for the isolated waste strip. The quench came from a reserved water tank and its separately funded valve, not from Yue's unprepared meridians. Its purpose was to cool the exposed scrap and reduce new attraction. It would not erase the charge already trapped in the creature. Yue listened for the exact task she could take while the stronger controls stayed with their operators.

foundry_creature_011.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_011.text: The apprentices could assist at three safe stations. One person would report the shield's fuel marks without guessing at the beast's intention. One would turn the ordinary shutter winch from a dry recess. One would keep the upper path clear and account for workers leaving it. Each station had a stop signal and a replacement. Yue's first pair remained quiet. A danger in front of her did not widen its recovered permission.

foundry_creature_012.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_012.text: Zhen took the evacuation tally until another worker relieved him.
