Yue chose a station by its ordinary demands, not by which one looked most like a cultivator fighting a spirit. The centipede struck the shield again, and the grounded edge flashed. Su Yan's voice stayed audible through the clash: say the mark, keep the path, stop at the signal. A small accurate task would help the whole defense more than an unmeasured attempt to become the strongest person there.

foundry_creature_choice.speaker: lin_yue
foundry_creature_choice.text: The barrier has finite fuel. My recovered first pair has no permission for a larger emergency pulse. I can report its gauge marks from the dry rail, help close the ordinary waste shutter from the recessed winch, or clear the upper access and count the workers who leave. Su Yan keeps the rated shield; the foreman keeps the quench valve. Each station has a replacement and a stop signal. I will choose the work I can actually perform.

choices.text: Report the barrier's remaining fuel marks.
Close the ordinary waste shutter from the dry winch.
Clear the upper access and account for departing workers.

foundry_gauge_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_gauge_001.text: Yue took the gauge station behind the dry rail. The shield's charge had fallen below the first reserve mark; its needle shook whenever a leg struck. She waited for the settled reading instead of calling the lowest flicker. Su Yan needed the actual remaining interval, not a dramatic version of it. Yue reported the mark and the last strike separately. The foreman began the quench sequence before the next replacement threshold.

foundry_gauge_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_gauge_002.text: Amber flecks moved along the centipede's armored seam. Yue wanted to use them as a second gauge. They belonged to the creature's uncertain stored charge, not the shield socket, and she could not measure them from the rail. She kept watching the instrument whose meaning she knew. The distinction felt narrow under fear. It left Su Yan with a trustworthy report rather than a guess disguised as spiritual perception.

foundry_gauge_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_gauge_003.text: The mark reached the agreed replacement line. Yue called it immediately, although the barrier still looked bright. A rested operator slid the next inspected socket into the rack while the frame remained supported. The used stone went to its discharge tray; it did not become a fresh reserve because the light had not quite died. Yue recorded the change and watched for the new settled reading.

foundry_gauge_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_gauge_004.text: By the stop signal, the quench was complete and the scrap source had cooled below its allowed attraction range. Yue left the gauge to her named replacement and stepped back. Her hands shook from ordinary fear. The report had helped the defense; the shaking was not proof that she had secretly strained a meridian. She kept both facts for the later check.

foundry_shutter_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_shutter_001.text: Yue took the recessed winch where stone shielded her from the seam. The shutter moved through ordinary gearing and carried no body load through her cuff. She checked the dry handle, waited for the foreman's signal and turned within the safe travel marks. A fragment stopped the last inch of closure. She reported the obstruction instead of forcing the handle or reinforcing the pull with qi.

foundry_shutter_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_shutter_002.text: A worker used the long clearing rod from the other sheltered station while Yue held the winch at its permitted stop. The task required timing and ordinary patience, not a higher stage. The centipede hit the distant shield, and the stone recess rang against her back. Yue nearly turned early. She waited for the clearing signal she could actually see, then completed the last inch.

foundry_shutter_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_shutter_003.text: The shutter seated against its inspected edge. A downstream trickle continued through the separate drain, exactly as the channel plan allowed. Yue did not announce that every path was closed. She named the scrap feed that had stopped and the drainage that remained. The foreman used that distinction to apply the quench without trapping water behind the wrong gate.

foundry_shutter_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_shutter_004.text: At the stop signal, Yue released the winch to its lock and moved behind the upper rail. Her shoulder stayed ordinary; her forearms ached from the handle. She had completed one mechanical task inside a larger cultivation defense. Wanting it to have been a spectacular strike would have added nothing to the seated shutter.

foundry_access_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_access_001.text: Yue took the upper path and moved the empty baskets from the stairs. She counted workers by the foreman's roll, asking each arrival to name the station they had left. A missing name did not necessarily mean someone had fallen; it did mean the foreman needed a precise question. Yue kept the doorway clear enough for that question to receive an answer.

foundry_access_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_access_002.text: One porter wanted to return for a sack of charcoal. Yue pointed to the supported shield and called the foreman rather than standing in his way alone. The sack could remain until the seam was safe; its ordinary value did not warrant another body in the channel. The porter waited angrily, then helped hold the upper door open for the last crew.

foundry_access_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_access_003.text: Zhen arrived with a second worker from the quench station. Their names closed the tally's gap, but Su Yan and the foreman still had work below. Yue marked them separately as protected operators remaining at named stations. A count that called everyone safe merely because the stairs were clear would have hidden the defense's unfinished task.

foundry_access_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_access_004.text: The stop signal brought the lower operators up through the path Yue had cleared. She handed the tally to the foreman and accepted relief from a rested worker. Her fear had not disappeared. It had acquired a task that could end. The count left nobody needing to perform another hazardous trip simply to satisfy an uncertain memory.

foundry_creature_rejoin_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_rejoin_001.text: The cooled waste no longer drew fresh bright flecks toward the scrap cup. Su Yan held the grounded shield while the adult centipede backed along the lower seam. Its own armor still carried residual charge, and its legs remained sharp. The crew waited rather than pursuing it into the opened downstream channel. The young followed under the spent shell. Nothing in that retreat promised the yard would never attract another creature.

foundry_creature_rejoin_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_rejoin_002.text: After the plated bodies passed the protected bend, the foreman closed apprentice access and set an ordinary inspection watch. The source had been isolated, the scrap cooled and the people counted. Those were completed facts. The creature's destination beyond the bend remained unknown. Su Yan shut down the shield only after its supported station could be vacated safely, then discharged the remaining socket into the emergency rack's inspected ground.

foundry_creature_rejoin_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_rejoin_003.text: The common debrief presented the settled fuel readings, shutter report and worker tally to every apprentice. Yue heard the reports whether she had stood at the gauge, winch or upper path. The account named each actual operator. Their combined evidence explained the defense without granting any one station knowledge it had not observed. The used stones and quench water were entered as genuine emergency costs.

foundry_creature_rejoin_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_rejoin_004.text: The barrier had consumed two finite socket charges, with one partly used reserve discharged after the retreat. The quench had drawn from the workshop's emergency water tank. The foreman scheduled replacement before reopening the hot waste line. Yue's quiet first pair contributed no sustained energy. Her ordinary station still belonged in the report. A cultivation defense could depend on a novice without pretending she had performed the examiner's higher-stage control.

foundry_creature_rejoin_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_rejoin_005.text: A small violet plate remained on the dry side of the seam where the adult had struck the barrier. Su Yan treated it as potentially charged material and kept hands away until the external blank and discharge checks passed. The plate had broken from armor; no whole spirit core lay inside it. The foreman recorded its custody with the workshop specimen account. Finding it did not make it Yue's possession or improve her root.

foundry_creature_rejoin_006.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_rejoin_006.text: Under isolation, the shed plate released charge through a long uneven tail resembling the stressed storage glaze. The similarity was useful and incomplete. A living creature's armor had a growth history unlike the kiln's cups. Su Yan permitted external comparison after cooling and forbade personal route use. Yue could study why it persisted without wearing it as a talisman or swallowing a powder made from its apparent value.

foundry_creature_rejoin_007.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_rejoin_007.text: The ordinary porter who had fallen received a wash-room check and a paid rest shift for his bruised heel. The emergency's end did not finish that care. Yue checked her own shoulder and hands under the existing recovery procedure; both remained ordinary after sleep. Her selected station had not widened her permission. The next cultivation attempt would still use the revised pad, a small dose and Su Yan's supervision.

foundry_creature_rejoin_008.speaker: narrator
foundry_creature_rejoin_008.text: Before reopening the yard, the foreman replaced the cracked scrap cover and changed the waste procedure. Cooling appearance alone no longer authorized disposal beside an active seam. Stored-charge fragments would be tested and grounded in a separated tray. The centipede had revealed a process problem, not bestowed a lesson designed for Yue. She could learn from it without imagining that every danger in the world existed to advance her.

foundry_resume_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_001.text: On Day Fifty-two, Yue returned to the comparison room after the yard's safety review. Her sleeping usable reserve was fourteen and a half units, above the former admission minimum and still short of the fourth-stage target. It had grown slowly before the failure and remained below its intended working load during rest. Su Yan would not treat the quiet field as evidence that the recovering shoulder could carry a larger task. Storage and route permission stayed separate.

foundry_resume_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_002.text: The first resumed second-route attempt used the revised warm-tested pad and the same tiny admission as before. Yue named the warming condition aloud. She felt the familiar forearm pressure, then the expected small delay. At the earliest change near the shoulder, she reported it. Su Yan ended the attempt, inspected the ordinary grip and marked the interrupted result as useful. Reporting had not ruined the lesson. It was the control the lesson existed to build.

foundry_resume_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_003.text: A later recovered attempt reached the provisional junction and returned through the unfinished upper-arm partner. The path did not yet match the full quarter-unit task. Yue could trace a small usable segment and stop without leaning on the first pair to finish it. Su Yan checked both returns separately. The diagram's two lines had begun to correspond to repeatable work, but the stage-four label remained unwritten. A partial circuit was still partial when it felt beautiful.

foundry_resume_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_004.text: The voidglass specimen sat behind an isolation cover at the other bench. Its fractured ribs held different residual tails in separate islands. Su Yan used it to demonstrate distributed storage, not to prescribe a human channel pattern copied from an animal. Yue's body had different tissue, different conversion and a different recovery history. The specimen could sharpen a question about timing. It could not become a shortcut to the second pair by resemblance.

foundry_resume_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_005.text: Yue asked whether separating the two returns in time would reduce the shoulder junction's crossflow. The examiner said that was already part of the prescribed successive test; the useful question was whether Yue actually waited for the first return to finish. Her spoken count had been faster when she was excited. They compared the count against an ordinary pendulum and found the difference. A small change in timing had masqueraded as a larger difference in spiritual readiness.

foundry_resume_006.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_006.text: They replaced the excited count with an audible workshop marker during supervised sessions. Outside those sessions, Yue rehearsed only the ordinary listening rhythm. The marker did not open a meridian for her. It made a timing condition reproducible while the body learned. Eventually she would need to interrupt without it. A teaching aid could support a skill without being mistaken for the skill itself.

foundry_resume_007.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_007.text: At the next small-dose attempt, she waited through the full return interval before beginning the new path. The shoulder pressure stayed lower. Su Yan changed no material and allowed no increased reserve that morning. The result supported timing as one factor, alongside the warm pad and recovered tissue. Yue wrote the narrower conclusion. She was finally learning not to turn a useful improvement into a theory that explained everything at once.

foundry_resume_008.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_008.text: Zhen tried the ordinary count beside her without opening his own unearned first pair. His stage-two practice remained quiet lower-field retention. He could still hear that Yue shortened the last interval when she anticipated success. He tapped the final beat gently on the table. She corrected it before the next supervised session. A lower-stage apprentice had supplied an observation the ninth-stage examiner could use, without either pretending their spiritual capacities were interchangeable.

foundry_resume_009.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_009.text: The ordinary morning shift now included a few carefully limited shoulder movements approved by the healer. Yue performed them at the start, then returned to low-table sorting. The check after work remained normal. A quiet teaching-room route would have to survive a realistic day, not merely a protected minute. The workshop adjusted the workload enough to prevent overuse and retained enough ordinary activity to make its examination meaningful.

foundry_resume_010.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_010.text: Every half-unit increase in retention followed a recovered overnight result at the previous level. Some mornings justified holding the target rather than increasing it. Yue stopped calling those mornings empty. They confirmed what the lower field could maintain under the actual work and weather. The compatible blend cost measured sampling charge and ordinary meals; it did not turn ambient qi into a limitless supply she could collect by refusing sleep.

foundry_resume_011.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_011.text: During the eighth week, the second pair carried an eighth-unit task with an inspected return. The first pair performed its own small task after full discharge. The succession stayed distinct at the shoulder junction. Yue wanted to combine them and feel the result of two routes at once. Su Yan covered the combined pattern on the chart. The fourth-stage assessment required separate control first; simultaneous work would need a later and narrower permission.

foundry_resume_012.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_012.text: She practiced interruption at deliberately inconvenient moments. Su Yan called stop before the pulse looked complete, after its admission settled and while Yue was naming the return. The unfinished feeling annoyed her. That was exactly the condition in which she needed reliable control. A route that stopped only when the practitioner felt satisfied could not be trusted near fatigue, surprise or an attractive next step.

foundry_resume_013.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_013.text: The ordinary healer's weekly shoulder check stayed normal. He approved a return to the old first-pair quarter-unit task under its familiar conditions. Yue performed it once, with the prepared external lead, then discharged. Recovering the former task did not mean the second pair could borrow its rating. She entered two separate permissions on the same page. The page looked slower than a single declaration of full recovery and was more useful at the bench.

foundry_resume_014.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_014.text: On Day Sixty-one, her reserve reached sixteen and a half usable units after the prescribed ordinary day and sleep. Compatibility remained above the method's minimum for the planned fourth-stage assessment. Su Yan repeated the sample with a fresh warm-condition blank before accepting it. A rising number could hide changing grit if they measured only quantity. Yue watched the fraction as carefully as the total.

foundry_resume_015.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_015.text: The second route's next increase was delayed by a humid afternoon. The material pad passed, but Yue's ordinary shoulder movement felt less settled after cup handling. She reported the difference before putting on the cuff. The examiner scheduled an unpowered inspection and held the practice dose. This time Yue did not need pain to make a limit persuasive. The delay cost a day in the schedule and protected a result the next attempt could actually interpret.

foundry_resume_016.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_016.text: That evening, the visiting merchant returned to the gate with a story about an apprentice elsewhere who had reached Foundation in a season. Yue listened long enough to ask which prior route records supported the story. He had no details. She wished the story were true in a way she could borrow. Then she paid for an ordinary packet of cloth and went back to the room. Other people's possible marvels did not settle her next examination.

foundry_resume_017.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_017.text: Su Yan knew practitioners with unusual roots and expensive protection who advanced much faster. She did not deny their existence to comfort Yue. Their circumstances were not Yue's. Some of their progress lasted; some concealed injuries that would become visible later. A cultivation system could contain exceptional cases without making ordinary work meaningless. Yue would be assessed against her demonstrated method, rather than required to become an exception before being worth teaching.

foundry_resume_018.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_018.text: The next recovered second-pair task reached the quarter-unit target. Its useful output cost more admission than the task itself delivered, and the loss stayed in the reserve account. Yue felt the new path's return finish distinctly from the first pair's familiar turn. Su Yan asked for immediate interruption on a fresh small pulse. Yue stopped cleanly. The route had performed a testable task, not yet survived the three recovered formal trials.

foundry_resume_019.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_019.text: At the end of the ninth week, she brought the complete record to the independent examiner who visited the foundry monthly. He was qualified for route assessment and had not supervised the practice. Su Yan supplied the material specifications and limits, including the failed warm-condition history. Yue supplied the reporting lapse. The visitor inspected the blanks and ordinary shoulder motion before scheduling a formal trial. Independence meant a different check of the evidence, not a guarantee of a favorable answer.

foundry_resume_020.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_020.text: He asked her to name what fourth stage would not permit. No leg route, no middle dantian, no sword aura, no flight, no patient healing and no sustained support beyond tested apparatus. Yue answered without treating the list as an insult. He asked what it would permit here. Two separately tested paired routes, better distribution within their allowances and carefully assessed transitions between them. The gain was specific enough to matter without becoming a promise of every power.

foundry_resume_021.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_021.text: On Day Sixty-seven, the sleeping field held seventeen and a half usable units. Yue left the next target at eighteen and spent the afternoon on ordinary ceramic inspection. She did not turn the last half-unit into a crisis requiring extra night practice. The food account, renewed bed and finite fuel remained in place through Day Eighty-four. There was room to fail the trial and review another term without pretending this one had no end.

foundry_resume_022.speaker: narrator
foundry_resume_022.text: The examination room had never looked grander than on the evening before the first formal trial. The shutters were ordinary timber. The sands in the grounding pot were dull. The old spoon rest held Zhen's brush. Yue had once wanted cultivation to carry her away from such things. Now she understood how many of them helped her attempt the next gate without gambling her hands. She folded the chart and went to supper while the room was still quiet.

foundry_assessment_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_001.text: On Day Seventy, Yue woke with eighteen and a quarter usable units retained after the prescribed ordinary day and sleep. The compatible fraction measured just above eighty-eight percent under independent sampling. The small sample's cost was entered before route work. The examiner checked a fresh blank and warmed reference pad himself. Su Yan stood outside the operator line, available to stop the apparatus but no longer supplying the judgment Yue hoped to hear.

foundry_assessment_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_002.text: The examiner chose the first pair's task before the second. Yue admitted its permitted pulse, performed the quarter-unit useful task and allowed the return to finish. The measured loss came out of her personal reserve. She named the completed discharge without waiting for praise. A familiar route could still fail under examination, particularly if she treated it as a formality before the more exciting new one.

foundry_assessment_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_003.text: He changed the order of the reference pads, leaving their specifications visible only in his own slate. Yue compared the blank rather than guessing which material ought to flatter her result. Its quiet response let the second-pair task proceed. The complementary path felt distinct at the forearm and shoulder. She completed the allowed useful pulse, then stopped before the old inward route began to anticipate another task.

foundry_assessment_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_004.text: Halfway through a fresh smaller admission, the examiner called stop. The unfinished sensation tugged at Yue's attention. She closed the input immediately and watched the return through its allowed interval. The instrument recorded a small tail within the corrected specification. Ordinary grip remained normal. The trial was provisionally complete. Next morning's sensation would decide whether that day's performance could remain in the qualifying set.

foundry_assessment_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_005.text: Yue returned to low-load sorting rather than repeating the successful pulse for anyone who asked to see it. Zhen congratulated her on the recorded work, not on a stage she had not received. At supper the lamps in the senior bay glowed brighter than her demonstration had. They did not diminish its value. She had met the particular test that mattered for her route under conditions another examiner could check.

foundry_assessment_006.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_006.text: On Day Seventy-one, the independent examiner and healer repeated ordinary touch and loaded shoulder movement. Both remained normal. The first trial stayed in the record. Yue asked whether they could count three demonstrations from the previous day as three trials. She knew the answer and wanted to hear why it held. Recovery separated the observations; repeating while already warmed and excited would not establish how the route returned after ordinary life and sleep.

foundry_assessment_007.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_007.text: They left a recovered interval before the second trial. Yue kept the same food, ordinary work and limited quiet practice rather than preparing a performance day unlike her usual schedule. The formal account named which loads were included. A heavier future shift might require smaller use even after advancement. The method's stage threshold was a demonstrated capacity under specified conditions, not a promise that every condition ahead would be equivalent.

foundry_assessment_008.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_008.text: On Day Seventy-four, the retained usable quantity measured eighteen and a half units with the compatible fraction still above the minimum. The examiner used a fresh warm-condition blank, then asked for the second pair first. Yue stopped a small admission at his early cue. Only after full discharge did she complete the rated second-route task. The changed sequence tested control rather than memory of yesterday's rehearsal.

foundry_assessment_009.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_009.text: The first pair followed after the shoulder junction returned to baseline. Its familiar path no longer felt entitled to interrupt the new one. Yue named its inlet, useful task and release separately. The external measuring strip agreed within its allowed timing. The two pairs had worked successively. No simultaneous circuit, unopened leg route or middle-dantian compression had been tested. The examiner wrote that limit next to the successful result.

foundry_assessment_010.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_010.text: During the ordinary afternoon check, Yue felt a dull ache in the forearm that frightened her. She reported it before deciding what it meant. The healer found ordinary fatigue consistent with the assigned ceramic handling and no altered touch or grip. He reduced the remaining work and retained the next-day examination. The ache was neither ignored nor automatically promoted into a cultivation injury. The second trial still required what tomorrow could show.

foundry_assessment_011.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_011.text: Day Seventy-five brought normal sensation and an ordinary loaded turn without the ache. The examiner accepted the second trial and noted the adjusted afternoon workload. Yue preferred the first trial's cleaner story. This result was less flattering and still sound because it recorded a symptom, investigation, work reduction and recovered check. She kept its full page rather than copying only the successful numbers into the front of the book.

foundry_assessment_012.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_012.text: For the final interval, Su Yan asked her to teach Zhen the external blank procedure using an empty cuff. She could explain material temperature, separate grounds and the reason for successive returns without borrowing qi from either body. Zhen supplied a deliberately misplaced well cover. Yue caught it after one uncertain glance. Teaching exposed where the explanation remained dependent on a familiar arrangement rather than a principle she could apply.

foundry_assessment_013.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_013.text: That evening she found an old page on which she had once written that reaching the first pair would make her a real cultivator. It was neither a lie nor a useful final definition. The first pair had made specific work possible. It had not completed her learning or replaced ordinary craft. She turned the page over and drafted what she wanted to preserve if the next examination failed: the recovered hands, the truthful record and the patience to continue.

foundry_assessment_014.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_014.text: On Day Seventy-nine, the third formal trial began under the same declared ordinary-day and sleep conditions. The reserve held eighteen and a quarter usable units, slightly below the second trial and safely above the target. Compatible charge remained above eighty-seven percent. Yue felt disappointment at the smaller total before recognizing that the method required stability, not a personal record every morning.

foundry_assessment_015.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_015.text: The examiner called interruption while she was explaining the second return. Yue stopped speaking long enough to close the admission, then finished the description after discharge. He asked why. She could divide attention only within the tested task; preserving a sentence was less important than the stop. Her route gave no special exemption from surprise because the cue came during an answer she understood well.

foundry_assessment_016.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_016.text: Both pairs completed their separate quarter-unit useful tasks within the corrected timing and material limits. The combined consumption left the reserve above its declared floor. The examiner closed the formal apparatus without allowing a triumphant extra pulse. Yue had completed the third provisionally qualifying trial. There would be another ordinary day, another sleep and another sensation check before the stage could change.

foundry_assessment_017.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_017.text: Rain began after supper. Yue stayed in the room with the cuff on its shelf, listening to the old floorboard knock. She could imagine the fourth-stage page filled in blue ink. She could also imagine waking with a numb finger. Neither imagined future deserved to replace the quiet evening she actually had. She ate the saved portion of rice and went to bed without performing a private examination that would complicate the morning's result.

foundry_assessment_018.speaker: narrator
foundry_assessment_018.text: On Day Eighty, ordinary touch, grip and shoulder movement remained normal. The healer signed the recovered check; the independent examiner compared all three qualifying pages, their blanks, interruptions and declared workloads. Only then did he enter Qi Gathering's fourth stage: Second pair. Yue read the line slowly. Nothing exploded above the bridge. Her hands still looked like the hands that had carried ash, mended cloth and once mistaken warmed copper for a trace.

foundry_earned_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_earned_001.text: The fourth-stage certificate named eighteen usable units, the compatible threshold, two separately tested pairs and their interruption limits. It did not declare every future day identical. Yue asked for a copy of the ordinary workload conditions to keep with it. The examiner gave her the whole record, including Day Thirty-one's failure. Her new capacity had grown through that history. Removing the embarrassing page would make the next teacher's inspection worse.

foundry_earned_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_earned_002.text: Su Yan permitted one quiet demonstration through the two already tested routes, successively with full discharge. The first turn felt like a known doorway; the second like a new path she could finally return from without borrowing the old one. On the external strip, jade and amber gave way to a separate copper-violet trace. The gaps remained visible. This was not the great circuit, and the open places were part of its earned shape.

foundry_earned_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_earned_003.text: Yue wanted to ask about the fifth stage before the second trace finished fading. She waited, discharged and asked afterward. Su Yan covered the next two limb pairs on the chart. Fourth stage provided their preparation's starting point, not permission to open both at once. They would need more reserve, compatible throughput, recovery and new tests. Yue found she could hear that without feeling the present achievement disappear.

foundry_earned_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_earned_004.text: At lunch, Zhen placed the old spoon rest beside her bowl and announced that it remained a spoon rest even in the presence of a fourth-stage practitioner. Yue laughed hard enough to spill a grain of rice. He remained at stage two. She knew how much his ordinary observations had helped her reach the page in her hand. She thanked him for specific things and bought no grand gift that would make their small exchange difficult to receive.

foundry_earned_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_earned_005.text: The foreman offered to move her at once to a higher furnace station. Yue asked for the station's ordinary loads, external controls and tested route requirements. They exceeded the fourth-stage tasks just certified. She accepted the smaller control bench instead, where a separate stone source powered the furnace and her routes could issue bounded commands after task-specific practice. The new stage made useful work possible. It did not make every offered job appropriate.

foundry_earned_006.speaker: narrator
foundry_earned_006.text: Above the ash channel, she read the certificate once more before putting it beside the patched work tablet. She had begun as a mortal wanting even a retained trace. She had earned a first pair, injured her confidence while preparing another, recovered and passed the next gate. The distance mattered. So did the bed, meals, craft teachers and truthful failures that had made it traversable. A cultivator's growth could be hers without having been hers alone.

foundry_aftermath_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_aftermath_001.text: On Day Eighty-one, the examiner inspected the small furnace control station she had accepted. The physical heat source was a measured stone charge; the manual shutter could end its supply independently of Yue's cuff. Her task would be a stopped command at a rated socket, never holding the furnace's heat in her body. The socket's position required a transition between the two routes. That transition had not been part of the formal stage test and needed its own low-dose practice.

foundry_aftermath_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_aftermath_002.text: Su Yan began the transition with the furnace cold and an isolated dummy load. Yue used the first pair's permitted command, discharged, repositioned the ordinary hand and used the second. The route change reduced an awkward shoulder turn. It did not remove ordinary fatigue or allow a longer pulse. The examiner watched the junction and the physical grip separately. A new stage had supplied a possible tool; learning its task was still work.

foundry_aftermath_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_aftermath_003.text: The dummy load's output measured lower than the useful quarter-unit task Yue had shown in examination. She accepted the smaller task without trying to make its light brighter for the foreman. A control signal needed a recognizable permitted response, not a spectacle. The separate furnace charge remained disconnected. Nobody would let a live heating load decide whether a novice's first attempt at a new transition was sound.

foundry_aftermath_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_aftermath_004.text: After a recovered check, she repeated the dummy command under the station's ordinary posture. The transition stayed within its allowed interval and released cleanly. The foreman approved one live command with Su Yan operating the main controls. Yue inspected the finite charge, watched the manual stop demonstrated and performed her small input. The chamber warmed through its own fuel. Her reserve paid for the command and its delivery loss, not the firing.

foundry_aftermath_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_aftermath_005.text: The ordinary batch took most of a day to finish. Yue's control task lasted moments. She spent the remaining shift checking cooling trays, recording fuel use and keeping the uncharged material separate from the personal-practice cupboard. The fourth-stage certificate did not make those hours beneath her. Its value was visible partly in how a short spiritual task could fit among ordinary work without consuming her whole body or hiding the furnace's real costs.

foundry_aftermath_006.speaker: narrator
foundry_aftermath_006.text: The first finished cup had a small glaze flaw near its foot. The foreman accepted it for ordinary use and kept it out of the rated practice batch. Yue examined the flaw with the same wooden tap she had learned as a third-stage newcomer. Advancement had not changed the clay's expansion rate or her duty to notice its particular limit. She set the cup on the restricted shelf and washed the inspection dust from her hands.

foundry_aftermath_007.speaker: narrator
foundry_aftermath_007.text: Zhen's stage-two retention had improved during the same weeks, but his first-pair preparation remained incomplete. He admitted envy after Yue's ceremony. She admitted wanting the senior's lamps even after earning her own next gate. They did not repair each feeling by denying the difference between their stages. They walked to supper together. His batch skills remained useful; her new route remained real. Neither fact required the other to become smaller.

foundry_aftermath_008.speaker: narrator
foundry_aftermath_008.text: Su Yan held the next paid-place review on Day Eighty-two, before the extension's last day. Yue could accept a further six weeks at the rated control bench, take a short cooling-material survey with a qualified crew, or finish the present term and leave with her wages and examination record. Each offer stated meals, ordinary load, fuel, travel and an end date. The workshop would not make continued training a reward available only to those who accepted its most hazardous work.

foundry_aftermath_009.speaker: narrator
foundry_aftermath_009.text: The control bench offered repetition and modest wages. The survey offered new materials under limits but required travel and an ordinary load assessment. Leaving offered time to visit home and send the full record to Duan Zhi before choosing another teacher. Yue wanted all three lives when she read them. A higher stage had made the choices wider, not made a day long enough to hold every possible practice.

foundry_aftermath_010.speaker: narrator
foundry_aftermath_010.text: The cooled voidglass fragment stayed in the workshop's specimen cupboard. Its external comparisons might help future storage designs, but personal route use remained forbidden. The foreman supplied an approved written extract for Yue's record. She did not offer the fragment as payment or a breakthrough prize. Yue appreciated the extract more after seeing how easily a striking object could draw her attention away from the conditions that made its study useful.

foundry_aftermath_011.speaker: narrator
foundry_aftermath_011.text: Before choosing, Yue stood under the ash bridge and reviewed what remained unfinished. The waste procedure needed ordinary inspection through the warm season. The porter needed another heel check. The new pad's warm-condition specification would need repetition on future batches. Her two routes needed the task limits kept with their certificate. None of that work vanished because she had reached a gate. Some belonged to her possible next job; some belonged to people who had accepted it.

foundry_aftermath_012.speaker: narrator
foundry_aftermath_012.text: She could choose a next step without promising to complete every remaining problem in the yard. The shared repair, recovery and examination records were already preserved with receiving workers named. Returning later would require renewed terms. Leaving today would not erase the work finished here. Yue opened the offers beside her spare return fare and made a decision with both the longing for progress and the body that had to live through it.

foundry_final_choice.speaker: lin_yue
foundry_final_choice.text: The second pair is earned, and its limits are still part of the record. I can accept another six weeks at the rated control bench, join the qualified crew's short cooling-material survey, or finish this paid term and travel home with the record and wages. Each offer has meals, ordinary loads, finite fuel and an end date. None promises the fifth stage. I will choose the next work without pretending that wanting all three gives me three bodies to do it.

choices.text: Join the qualified crew's cooling-material survey.
Finish the paid term and take the record home.

foundry_bench_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_bench_001.text: Yue accepted the further six-week control-bench term after the foreman read its limits aloud. Work would begin after the current place ended, with review before the new final shift. The furnace account supplied measured charges; the ordinary meal account supplied food. Her personal sampling and command costs stayed in the practice ledger. The offer purchased scheduled work, not unrestricted access to every hot chamber in the yard.

foundry_bench_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_bench_002.text: On the first new morning, she inspected the dummy socket again rather than relying on the inspection from her demonstration. A loose ordinary fastener had appeared during a cooling cycle. The socket remained unpowered until the mechanic tightened it and repeated the ground check. Yue had earned the second pair, not immunity from a fastener. Su Yan countersigned the task's conditions before the live shift began.

foundry_bench_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_bench_003.text: The first pair issued one rated command, then discharged. Yue moved her ordinary hand to the next control position and used the second pair's separately tested return. The transition spared the old shoulder twist. It did not spare the need to inspect the material pad at cuff temperature. She kept the new heat sink clear of ash with an unpowered brush before another session.

foundry_bench_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_bench_004.text: Her first week's useful outputs were small enough to fit on one slate. The furnace's fuel consumption filled a larger column. The difference pleased her. She could now help control work beyond what her own reserve could power while leaving the real energy source visible. Greater cultivation had made a bounded contribution more precise, rather than making every large result proof of her personal strength.

foundry_bench_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_bench_005.text: Zhen brought a fresh spoon rest for the bench's tools and kept the old one for his brush. He asked Yue to inspect a glaze seam at its foot. She made the ordinary comparison, found the piece sound for its intended use and thanked him. He still practiced stage-two retention after supper. She still waited between her two tested returns. They had changed at different speeds while continuing to share a table.

foundry_bench_006.speaker: narrator
foundry_bench_006.text: Before the first weekly review, Su Yan asked which fifth-stage lesson Yue wanted next. Yue named the additional limb-pair preparation, then asked for the prerequisites, costs and recovery intervals before any diagram was uncovered. The question sounded cautious and ambitious at the same time. She could want the next gate without treating the present term as a promise that it would open.

foundry_survey_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_survey_001.text: Yue accepted the short survey after its qualified leader checked her ordinary carrying load. The crew would inspect cooling-material seams for five days, with a receiving station, return transport and finite reference fuel. Her role was surface comparison within the two pairs' tested limits. She would neither enter a live furnace seam nor act as the crew's ward operator. The offer paid travel and food separately from any useful specimens found.

foundry_survey_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_survey_002.text: They left the workshop with a sealed reference kit, uncharged tools and no voidglass fragment. The written specimen extract stayed in Yue's book. At the first roadside kiln, she used ordinary observation to identify a glaze shape resembling the thick cups. Resemblance established a candidate, not a result. The crew obtained the keeper's sampling terms before cutting a small external test piece.

foundry_survey_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_survey_003.text: A cool-condition comparison gave a short tail. Warmed to its actual handling condition, the same piece answered longer. Yue reported both without calling the roadside kiln guilty of the foundry's exact failure. Its firing history and intended use differed. The crew kept the sample out of personal route work and wrote a local storage limit. A lesson learned elsewhere had supplied a question whose answer still belonged to this place.

foundry_survey_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_survey_004.text: On the third day, ordinary carrying tired her calves. The newly earned second pair still opened no leg channel. She put down the kit and accepted a turn carrying lighter slates while another worker took the tools. The survey schedule allowed ordinary rest. Using cultivation well included declining a task its actual anatomy could not support, even when the road made a reinforced stride look attractive.

foundry_survey_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_survey_005.text: The fifth day's final comparison left reference fuel unused. The leader recorded it for return to the workshop account rather than treating the remainder as a private practice allowance. Yue received pay for the completed survey and copies of the permitted findings. She had learned three new material questions and earned no additional stage. The survey ended with a return, a meal and a next-day hand check.

foundry_survey_006.speaker: narrator
foundry_survey_006.text: Back at the ash bridge, Su Yan read the warm-condition findings beside the foundry specification. Some confirmed its limits; one suggested a different source of a long tail. They would need future tests before changing apprentice practice. Yue liked that her report could leave work unfinished and still be useful. The north road beyond the workshop no longer looked like an escape from careful details. It held more of them.

foundry_home_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_home_001.text: Yue chose to finish the current term and travel home before accepting more work. The foreman paid the completed wages, returned the drawer deposit and supplied the whole examination record. The workshop kept its instruments and specimen. Yue kept her patched cuff, ordinary clothes and earned capacity. She could feel affection for the ash bridge without turning affection into a duty to remain until every difficult batch was solved.

foundry_home_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_home_002.text: She paid the return fare from the copper reserved before admission. There was enough for meals and a modest repair packet for her mother's roof tiles, with a little left for a future courier. The calculation had changed through completed work, not through an imagined fifth-stage wage. At the gate, Zhen gave her the old spoon rest after drying his brush elsewhere. She accepted the small gift without promising a grand return.

foundry_home_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_home_003.text: On the road, she practiced no new route. Her second pair remained available only within its tested task and recovery conditions; travel added ordinary fatigue that the foundry examination had not measured exhaustively. At an inn she completed the permitted quiet check, discharged and slept. Reaching home sooner did not justify turning the ordinary road into an unsupported test of speed.

foundry_home_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_home_004.text: Her mother met her beside the kiln shed where the old vent still warmed the wall. Yue laid out the certificate and the repaired work tablet. Her mother asked to see her hands before reading either. Both moved ordinarily. Yue found herself describing the failed warm pad before the successful trials. The order made the achievement less polished and the journey easier for someone who cared about the body rather than the title.

foundry_home_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_home_005.text: They cooked rice well away from the vent that had once spoiled it. Yue had gained four Qi Gathering stages since the years when she could retain none. Her mother's ordinary heat had changed no less and no more than it had before. She gave the roof repair packet and sent a paid copy of the record to Duan Zhi. No pendant opened, no secret inheritance arrived and no household task vanished in the presence of a cultivator.

foundry_home_006.speaker: narrator
foundry_home_006.text: At supper, her mother asked whether she would continue. Yue said yes, then named the money, teachers, materials and recovered tests she would need before the next pair. The answer was longer than a vow and smaller than a legend. She slept in the familiar room with the certificate on a dry shelf. Tomorrow would begin with ordinary food, ordinary chores and a body worth preserving for the cultivation still ahead.

foundry_end_survey.speaker: narrator
foundry_end_survey.text: The survey kit returned with unused fuel, permitted samples and a record of warm and cool comparisons. Yue's hands remained ordinary after the last night's sleep. At the ash bridge she read the new questions beside the failed pad that had once frightened her. The fourth stage had helped her ask them more precisely; it had not supplied every answer. Beyond the settling channel, a road climbed toward other workshops. She could follow it with food, a receiving place and limits that traveled as carefully as her ambition.

foundry_end_home.speaker: narrator
foundry_end_home.text: At home, Yue set the spoon rest beneath an ordinary work brush. The fourth-stage certificate stayed dry beside the patched tablet. Her mother's repaired roof still needed inspection after rain, and rice still needed the right distance from the kiln vent. Cultivation had changed what Yue could carry through her two tested routes. It had not made the familiar household disappear. She slept with a plan for the next teacher, paid copper for the next journey and hands that could still take up tomorrow's work.

foundry_home_007.speaker: narrator
foundry_home_007.text: Her mother spoke of the lake without opening the jade. The old technique's cost had not been restored by the passing years; ordinary work remained fitted around the damaged route. Yue's new pair could not repair it. The afternoon beside the star had been an offered kindness with a price, not evidence of a superior family root. Her mother could still teach clay, herb labels and ordinary breath. Safe internal-route instruction had required teachers whose present methods and capacity could be inspected.

foundry_home_008.speaker: narrator
foundry_home_008.text: 'I should have explained more before you left,' her mother said. 'I told you the pendant was a memory and where to take it when travel was safe. I avoided the cost because I could not bear making it the first thing you inherited from me. Silence did not make it safer.' Yue kept that admission beside Yun's different delay. Neither account made the years simple. It did let them speak now without pretending someone had stolen a memory from either of them.

foundry_home_009.speaker: narrator
foundry_home_009.text: Yue described the manual escape, the star's confirmed terms and the qualified operators who had carried the mountain's load. Her part had used a tested first-stage relay. She did not offer a claim to have healed the star or solved the lost years. Her mother listened, then set the rice bowls down with both ordinary hands. The account belonged to work already completed under whichever support plan the mountain had taken. At home, its meaning could remain personal without becoming a new cultivation technique.

foundry_refinery_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_refinery_001.text: Before personal sampling, Su Yan took the apprentices to the cold refining furnace. Five small reference containers stood outside its chamber, each sealed behind an independent inlet. Mixing their contents together would not make a five-phase root. The external apparatus could combine permitted fractions for a particular test. A body still needed its own conversion and return to be examined. Yue read the inlet paths before asking to see them powered.

foundry_refinery_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_refinery_002.text: The examiner placed a known wood-compatible fraction beside a metal-compatible one and drew their local conversion relation on an unpowered slate. The labels belonged to a taught method with specified materials. They did not license arbitrary household ash or a bright mineral bought by name alone. Zhen supplied two ordinary powders that looked like the references. The external comparison distinguished them; the surface colors did not.

foundry_refinery_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_refinery_003.text: One trade sample amplified the reference's first flash while lengthening its tail. Another dimmed the flash and returned promptly. Yue initially called the brighter sample stronger. Su Yan asked stronger for which task. A storage cup might value persistence; an interruption lesson needed release. The word had concealed the question they actually needed to answer. Yue crossed it out and named the output and duration separately.

foundry_refinery_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_refinery_004.text: At the cold furnace's socket, a senior adjusted the material fractions without feeding the main chamber. His control required a route rating above Yue's current task. She could observe the physical shutter and record the settled comparison. She could not imitate his internal path because the exterior result looked simple. Some of the most dangerous work in a cultivation workshop wore the appearance of a quiet hand moving very little.

foundry_refinery_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_refinery_005.text: The senior used a prepared reference circle to hold the external fractions apart. Every segment had a return; every return met a visible ground. Su Yan opened one segment with the source off and asked the apprentices what would happen on admission. Zhen identified the interrupted return before Yue did. The fact pleased the examiner. Recognizing a diagram error was ordinary learned craft and did not require Zhen to pretend he had opened Yue's first pair.

foundry_refinery_006.speaker: narrator
foundry_refinery_006.text: With the return repaired and inspected, the external circle ran for a timed interval on its own stone supply. The source gauge fell while the reference remained almost constant. A steady light was not a steady reserve. Yue wrote the gauge marks at the beginning and end. The apparatus had spent charge maintaining a comparison that looked unchanged. Future talisman work would need this account as surely as a momentary wick needed its measured dose.

foundry_refinery_007.speaker: narrator
foundry_refinery_007.text: Su Yan named the difference between an admitted trace, refined compatible qi and useful output at a task. Each transition could lose quantity or change what remained. The word purity described compatibility within a method, not a person's worth. Yue had heard ordinary mixed roots dismissed as dirty. The reference showed why that insult supplied no useful measurement. A practitioner could deserve careful teaching while converting inefficiently.

foundry_refinery_008.speaker: narrator
foundry_refinery_008.text: The five fractions also changed one another's return. A little of one could soften an uneven tail; too much could introduce another delay. The interaction was tested in the isolated apparatus before anyone proposed a personal blend. No universal five-color recipe could settle every body, batch and temperature. Yue's future small sample would be a question asked under these controls, rather than a request that the comb choose a destiny.

foundry_refinery_009.speaker: narrator
foundry_refinery_009.text: She asked whether a better refining flame could make every material safe. Su Yan showed a cracked cup after its surface residue had burned away. Some impurities could be removed; the body crack remained. Higher heat could also alter a material's useful phase or consume the very fraction they meant to preserve. A furnace could improve a specified process. It could not repeal every difference between unsuitable and suitable material.

foundry_refinery_010.speaker: narrator
foundry_refinery_010.text: One apprentice had heard that an alchemist could purify anything through force of intent. The examiner did not claim that intention played no part in a cultivator's control. She asked how the alleged process would be compared, interrupted and checked afterward. The apprentice had only a story. They left room in the notebook for evidence if it arrived. They did not put Yue's body into that empty space to find out.

foundry_refinery_011.speaker: narrator
foundry_refinery_011.text: Su Yan allowed the students to inspect a sealed specimen of condensed teaching fluid supplied by a Foundation practitioner. Yue could see its slow surface movement without receiving any into her field. It was compatible with its owner's liquid-reservoir method, not automatically with a Qi Gathering novice. Swallowing or admitting it would be a load her gaseous field had no tested means to carry.

foundry_refinery_012.speaker: narrator
foundry_refinery_012.text: The specimen led her to ask what actually separated Qi Gathering's great circuit from Foundation. The answer named balanced vessel bridges, controlled compression and prepared recovery, not merely a larger reserve. A gaseous field could hold more without safely becoming a liquid reservoir. Foundation's eight pillars would require their own long tests. Yue closed the specimen's cover without imagining a shortcut concealed in its shine.

foundry_refinery_013.speaker: narrator
foundry_refinery_013.text: Su Yan had reached the ninth Qi Gathering stage and had not yet attempted Foundation compression. She explained that her great-circuit tests were sound but the prepared recovery place and method compatibility remained incomplete. Being able to teach Yue did not mean being finished herself. Yue watched the examiner's steady hands with a new feeling. Even a much higher gate could be approached through declared unfinished work rather than a public performance of certainty.

foundry_refinery_014.speaker: narrator
foundry_refinery_014.text: The senior student asked whether postponing Foundation diminished the examiner's authority. Su Yan set her teaching specifications beside the unanswered compression requirements. She was qualified to inspect the former and had not claimed the latter. Confusing them would endanger both teacher and pupil. Yue recognized another version of the distinction she needed for herself: an earned first pair could support useful work without granting an unopened second.

foundry_refinery_015.speaker: narrator
foundry_refinery_015.text: After the isolated refining demonstration, each reference container returned to its own storage. Unused fuel stayed in the socket account. The students washed ordinary dust from the benches before bringing any personal sample near the comb. Yue understood why the morning had included so much cold and unpowered work. A wrong physical path could turn a spiritual test into a question about the apparatus instead of the body.

foundry_refinery_016.speaker: narrator
foundry_refinery_016.text: At the lesson's end, she wrote a small diagram of the process: specified material, controlled input, inspected transformation, observed return, recovery. The diagram was not a talisman. Its lines carried no qi. She kept it because it would stop her from collapsing several difficult questions into the bright word cultivation. When Su Yan called the first personal sampling group, Yue finally knew what she was going there to learn.

foundry_martial_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_martial_001.text: Between material sessions, Su Yan brought Yue to dry boards behind the foundry. Two ordinary practice staffs lay beside an inspected cuff-to-sole conducting stitch. The boards were level and the boundary rope slack. A prepared reinforced movement could be taught here without the wet turn of the ash channel. Yue's first pair had already earned that limited task at the sluice; the foundry would inspect the new conditions before permitting it.

foundry_martial_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_martial_002.text: She began with the field closed, feet moving around chalk marks. Su Yan used the staff to show where an ordinary strike could arrive if Yue turned late. The examiner did not need sword aura to make the position matter. Yue's old kiln stance planted her weight firmly and made a retreat awkward. She repeated the empty-handed turn until the teacher could change the cue without finding the same planted heel.

foundry_martial_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_martial_003.text: Zhen joined the ordinary drill with no powered cuff. His stage-two retention supplied no internal first pair, but his work around fragile trays had taught him to stop without upsetting a load. He crossed the chalk turn more smoothly than Yue. She wanted to blame the movement on his lighter build. Su Yan asked her to watch the timing she could actually learn. Weight was a condition; it was not an excuse to ignore a better ordinary step.

foundry_martial_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_martial_004.text: The first exercise ended with Yue off balance and the staff's padded tip against her sleeve. She had watched Su Yan's hand instead of the route available to her feet. The teacher held the tip still until Yue named the open retreat. No bruise was needed. A missed answer in slow ordinary practice could become a fall if she tried to repair it later with a stronger pulse.

foundry_martial_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_martial_005.text: After the ordinary baseline, Su Yan inspected the conducting stitch from cuff to sole. Its external path did not open a leg meridian. The quarter-unit useful support would travel through a rated cloth route supplied by the first arm pair, with the current delivery loss charged to Yue's reserve. They checked the ground and release at the dry board. A technique name did not remove the preparation hidden beneath it.

foundry_martial_006.speaker: narrator
foundry_martial_006.text: Yue performed one aligned reinforced step, discharged and stood still. The sole received the permitted brief support; her ordinary knee and hip supplied the direction. It was not a jump over the channel. Su Yan examined the turn afterward and found the same tendency to plant the heel when excited. Spiritual reinforcement had made the prepared movement more decisive without fixing the ordinary movement after it.

foundry_martial_007.speaker: narrator
foundry_martial_007.text: They removed the cuff and returned to the chalk. Yue disliked doing so after the bright success. The examiner asked which fact the pulse had changed. It had supported one step. It had not taught a safe follow-through. Zhen tapped the next chalk mark and waited. Yue repeated the unpowered turn until it no longer felt like an apology for being a third-stage practitioner.

foundry_martial_008.speaker: narrator
foundry_martial_008.text: On a recovered morning, Su Yan added the staff cue before the permitted step. Yue recognized it, moved through the aligned route and discharged before turning. Her hand remained normal and the ordinary stance recovered without the planted heel. The result justified one small practiced combination. It did not justify a second reinforced step on the same admission or a longer route through the legs she had not opened.

foundry_martial_009.speaker: narrator
foundry_martial_009.text: A senior apprentice offered a short ordinary sparring round after the lesson. He held the fourth stage but agreed to keep both fields closed. Yue accepted after Su Yan checked the padded staffs and limited the round. She lost the first exchange when she reached too far. The senior's better distance, not an unannounced realm advantage, had found her. She could learn the error without searching for a hidden channel explanation.

foundry_martial_010.speaker: narrator
foundry_martial_010.text: In the second exchange she kept the better stance and saw the opening, then hurried toward it. The padded tip reached her sleeve again. Wanting a visible victory had shortened her ordinary timing as effectively as wanting a route had shortened the count at the bench. Yue asked for a slower repeat instead of a stronger circuit. The senior demonstrated the gap she had left and let her step through it without a contest.

foundry_martial_011.speaker: narrator
foundry_martial_011.text: She declined a powered round that afternoon. The approved Reed-Step combination had its own quiet conditions, and sparring would add surprise, load and fatigue they had not examined together. The senior accepted the refusal without calling it cowardice. Yue still felt cowardly for a moment. Naming an appropriate limit did not guarantee that pride would approve it before the body benefited.

foundry_martial_012.speaker: narrator
foundry_martial_012.text: At the wall she found an old practice diagram of a projected sword edge. Its note named Golden Core's controlled turns and a grounded blade. She read the requirement instead of copying the light shape into her own sleeve. Shen Qing's teaching blade had used separate protections at the sluice. Neither that demonstration nor her fourth-stage opponent's ordinary staff gave her permission for sword aura.

foundry_martial_013.speaker: narrator
foundry_martial_013.text: Su Yan described how later routes could support repeated movement when their tissue, returns and reserve had been inspected. Foundation could sustain reinforcement over longer tasks; a prepared artifact could add its own support. Each gain would alter the conditions worth practicing. None would make distance judgment irrelevant. Yue found it possible to imagine great cultivation while still seeing why today's chalk mark remained worth her attention.

foundry_martial_014.speaker: narrator
foundry_martial_014.text: The merchant who sold quickening powder watched from outside the practice boundary. He offered to sponsor a wager against the senior, citing Yue's determination. The padded lesson had become a proposed contest with money attached. Su Yan required separate terms and a qualified assessment before any powered match. Yue declined the wager. Her meals already had an account; she did not need to make an injury profitable to someone watching.

foundry_martial_015.speaker: narrator
foundry_martial_015.text: Zhen asked afterward whether refusing a wager had made the lesson less brave. Yue said she had wanted the audience to see her win more than she had wanted a sound test. Admitting that disappointed her. It also made the merchant's offer easier to understand. The man had noticed a feeling he could sell back to her as an opportunity.

foundry_martial_016.speaker: narrator
foundry_martial_016.text: They ended with one ordinary sequence repeated correctly and no additional powered dose. Yue recorded the earlier reinforced task, its delivery loss, the closed-field sparring and the next-day check it would still need. Martial practice entered the same notebook as material practice. Different tasks shared one body and one reserve. A beautiful account of courage would not help the examiner interpret a sore shoulder if it omitted what she had actually done.

foundry_martial_017.speaker: narrator
foundry_martial_017.text: Next morning her hands and shoulder remained normal under the ordinary inspection. The dry-board task stayed permitted under its tested conditions. She took the cuff apart for cleaning and left it on its rated shelf before going to the cup benches. Yue could now name both the power she had used and the skill it had not supplied. The distinction made cultivation richer than the single word strength she had once brought to the recruitment gate.

foundry_nights_001.speaker: narrator
foundry_nights_001.text: During the renewed place's first quiet evening, Yue read the oldest page of her work tablet. It recorded a mortal's meals and ordinary shifts, with no retained qi to measure. She had once imagined that page becoming embarrassing after advancement. The recent failure made it useful again. The body that now carried a first pair was the same body whose food, sleep and work had first made a repeatable trace possible.

foundry_nights_002.speaker: narrator
foundry_nights_002.text: She had spent seven years wanting cultivation before the terrace admitted her to paid training. Some of those years had taught patience; others had taught the habit of hiding disappointment. At the foundry, hiding could make a missed return difficult to report. The old desire was neither a pure virtue nor a curse. Yue could keep the part that brought her to the bench and train the part that wanted a flattering record more than a usable one.

foundry_nights_003.speaker: narrator
foundry_nights_003.text: A night's dream gave her a completed great circuit. In it, every line on the chart opened when she looked at it, and the chimney contractions answered like distant bells. She woke with an ordinary cramped shoulder from sleeping badly. No route had opened. The healer checked the posture and kept the resting limits unchanged. Yue wrote the dream in a private margin so it would not accidentally become part of the examination history.

foundry_nights_004.speaker: narrator
foundry_nights_004.text: The dream embarrassed her less than the wish beneath it. She wanted to arrive somewhere that could no longer tell her to begin again. Su Yan answered that no realm she knew abolished every beginning. New tasks could exceed old tests; a damaged vessel could require repair; a teacher could reach a limit. Higher cultivation would make more kinds of work possible. It would also make some mistakes more costly.

foundry_nights_005.speaker: narrator
foundry_nights_005.text: Zhen asked what she would do if the second pair never became usable. Yue first answered that she would try harder, then heard how little the phrase specified. She could seek another qualified method, examine compatibility, continue rated work and decide what further risk she accepted. Those decisions were not all available today, and none guaranteed success. The answer left room for persistence without making her body an enemy to defeat.

foundry_nights_006.speaker: narrator
foundry_nights_006.text: He said that his own stage-two field might be enough for the ordinary career he wanted. Yue struggled not to hear that as surrender. Zhen could improve his craft, support the kiln household he hoped to build and still choose whether to pursue a first pair later. His ambitions did not have to match hers to be serious. She found that accepting his choice made her own desire easier to describe without demanding that everyone share it.

foundry_nights_007.speaker: narrator
foundry_nights_007.text: The foreman brought an ordinary repair request to the room: a drawer latch that stuck when its wooden runner swelled. Yue could mend it without loading the resting shoulder. She planed the runner slowly and fitted a small dry spacer. No qi entered the task. Finishing it returned a pleasure that the route failure had pushed aside. She could still do useful things while the most wanted thing waited.

foundry_nights_008.speaker: narrator
foundry_nights_008.text: After the latch moved cleanly, she returned the tools and asked the foreman to check its travel. The independent check found a sharp edge she had missed. Yue smoothed it and received the modest repair credit. The sequence felt familiar in a reassuring way: a task, a limit, another person's observation and a correction. Cultivation had made that sequence more intricate, not invented it in a life that previously held nothing.

foundry_nights_009.speaker: narrator
foundry_nights_009.text: Her mother's reply arrived with a plain account of the kiln's damp firewood. She asked whether Yue still put rice too near a hot vent when absorbed in a notebook. The remembered ordinary failure made Yue laugh. She answered that the foundry kept food away from samples and that she was resting an unfinished route. She did not ask her mother to make a promise about its recovery that no letter could support.

foundry_nights_010.speaker: narrator
foundry_nights_010.text: Su Yan read with her at the comparison-room table while the cuff stayed in its drawer. They studied the difference between an interrupted pair and a bridge ready for a heavenly circuit. The words could be understood without rehearsing them in the body. Yue asked whether reading itself could contaminate practice by making her expect a sensation. 'It can,' Su Yan said. 'That is why we keep your report separate from the pattern you hope it resembles.'

foundry_nights_011.speaker: narrator
foundry_nights_011.text: The next lesson had no personal sample. Yue listened to a known external trace through an ordinary sounding cup, then to a blank. One note came from the cup's physical vibration; the other from the controlled comparison. She initially combined them. The examiner changed the cup and preserved the trace condition. The changed ordinary note exposed the mixture in her expectation. Spiritual attention needed controls because ordinary senses still contributed to what she thought she knew.

foundry_nights_012.speaker: narrator
foundry_nights_012.text: She learned to say 'I do not know which part I felt' without ending the inquiry. Su Yan could adjust a control, repeat a permitted observation or stop until conditions improved. Certainty manufactured to avoid embarrassment would remove those options. Yue remembered the one-breath delay at the shoulder. The same small habit could grow from an uncertain sentence into a harmful attempt if she never practiced telling the truth at the easier scale.

foundry_nights_013.speaker: narrator
foundry_nights_013.text: At night, the senior apprentice left a lamp outside the room without asking Yue to discuss her progress. Its ordinary flame needed oil and a trimmed wick. She could read one page, finish supper and put it out. The modest gift had a simpler shape than encouragement she had to repay with a successful examination. Yue used it for the revised material report and slept when the report was read.

foundry_nights_014.speaker: narrator
foundry_nights_014.text: The next morning's hand check stayed ordinary. The rest interval had not ended, and the second route still carried no permission. Yet Yue felt less as if the closed page had erased her cultivation. She had practiced attention, repaired a drawer, accepted help and described a limit more accurately. Those were not hidden stages awarded in consolation. They were conditions that could let the earned stages remain useful when practice resumed.
